description: Configuration for the ERPNext MCP server: the master switch, the token an AI client authenticates with, the network allowlist, and one switch per tool.

fields.description: Master switch. While this is off the MCP endpoint answers 404 for everyone, whatever else is configured here. This is the fastest way to cut off an AI client: untick, save, done — no restart, no token change.
fields.label: Enabled

fields.description: Token an MCP client must present, as X-MCP-Token (or Authorization: Bearer where the site's OAuth layer leaves it alone). Generated by the button below; stored encrypted and never shown again, logged or returned by any tool. Treat it as read access to your entire general ledger.
fields.label: Auth Token

fields.description: When the current token was created. Rotate it if it may have leaked.
fields.label: Token Generated On
Endpoint
fields.options:
Endpoint
POST https://<your-site>/api/method/erpnext_mcp.mcp.handle

Header
X-MCP-Token: <token>

JSON-RPC 2.0 (MCP Streamable HTTP). POST only — this server sends no unsolicited messages, so there is no stream to open.

Every call, allowed or refused, is recorded in MCP Action Log.

fields.description: The config an MCP client needs, generated from this site's own URL and token. The preview is masked; Copy and Download fetch the real token separately, so this panel is safe to leave open on a shared screen.
fields.label: Connect to Claude Desktop

fields.description: Comma- or newline-separated CIDR blocks allowed to reach the endpoint, checked after the token. Defaults to loopback plus private LAN ranges. An empty list denies everyone — a blank field is far more often a mistake than an intent to publish an accounting API. Add 0.0.0.0/0 only if you genuinely mean the whole internet.
fields.label: Allowed CIDRs

fields.description: Base URL a client should use, if it differs from the one this site sees. Leave empty and the connection panel uses frappe.utils.get_url(). Set it for a site behind a Tailscale Funnel, a tunnel or a reverse proxy on another hostname — there is no way for the server to guess its own public name. Example: https://erp.tail1234.ts.net
fields.label: Public URL

fields.description: On: the Farm Ops mobile app can reach /api/method/erpnext_mcp.api.mobile.* and .../erpnext_mcp.api.files.* with a per-user API token. Off: every one of those eleven methods answers 503 immediately, for every phone, without reading or writing anything — the one-flip shutdown for the mobile surface. This is SEPARATE from the master switch above, which governs the MCP endpoint the AI uses: stopping the AI and stopping the phones are different decisions. It can also be forced off without the Desk by setting "farm_ops_mobile_enabled": 0 in site_config.json; either source saying off means off.
fields.label: Farm Ops Mobile API Enabled

fields.description: Days a Farm Ops credential may go unused before a nightly sweep revokes its token. This is what limits the damage from a phone lost in an orchard and never reported: an unreported device stops working by itself. The ACCOUNT is never disabled and the roles and entity access are untouched — only the token goes, and the worker gets a new QR. Tick "Exempt From Idle Sweep" on a Mobile Access Grant that is legitimately quiet for months. Set this to 0 to switch the sweep off entirely.
fields.label: Revoke Idle Mobile Credentials After (Days)

fields.description: Where the weekly Journal Entry attribution drift report goes when it finds something. Comma-separated; leave empty and it goes to every enabled System Manager on the site. The watch is READ-ONLY — it reports drift and never repairs it, because rewriting GL rows on submitted accounting documents on a timer is not something this app does. If no outgoing email account is configured the report lands in the Error Log instead, so a finding is never lost to an SMTP setting.
fields.label: Drift Report Recipients

fields.description: On: tools run as the MCP System User below, so every document an AI created carries an owner that is obviously not a person, and every permission-checked tool (reports, attachments, comments, workflow actions) is bounded by that user's roles. Off: they run as Administrator, which works but makes MCP-authored documents indistinguishable from an admin's own. Leave this on unless you have a specific reason.
fields.label: Attribute Actions To An MCP System User

fields.description: The user tools run as, and that mutations are attributed to. Create a dedicated one (for example mcp@yourcompany.example) with only the roles the tools you enabled actually need — Accounts User is normally enough for the ledger tools; reports, attachments and workflow actions need whatever their own DocTypes require. Falls back to Administrator if left empty.
fields.label: MCP System User

fields.description: Search, group and bulk-set the tool switches below. Every switch is still here and still individual — this only makes the seven hundred of them navigable. A preset writes every tool switch at once and touches nothing else on this form.
fields.label: Tool Permissions

fields.description: All on by default; none of these can change data. Turning one off removes it from the catalogue entirely, so a client cannot see it. Use this to keep an AI's view down to the job it is doing.
fields.label: Accounting Read Tools

fields.description: Map companies, cost centers, fiscal years and chart-of-accounts roots. The orientation call every client should make first.
fields.label: Get Company Topology

fields.description: Balance of one account as of a date, summed from GL Entry.
fields.label: Get Account Balance

fields.description: Paginated Journal Entry headers by date range, company, account and docstatus.
fields.label: Get Journal Entries

fields.description: One Journal Entry with every account line, party and reference.
fields.label: Get Journal Entry

fields.description: READ. Diagnostic: every line of one Journal Entry beside every GL Entry row it posted, with the join spelled out and every disagreement flagged. Explains why a party edit matched no ledger rows.
fields.label: Investigate JE/GL Link

fields.description: Bank Transactions by account, date range and status.
fields.label: List Bank Transactions

fields.description: One Bank Statement, where this ERPNext version has the doctype.
fields.label: Get Bank Statement

fields.description: Fiscal years and the companies they apply to.
fields.label: List Fiscal Years

fields.description: The chart of accounts as a nested tree.
fields.label: Get Chart Of Accounts

fields.description: Bank Transactions with money still unallocated.
fields.label: List Unreconciled Bank Transactions

fields.description: Fuzzy account lookup by number or name. Turn this off and a client must know exact docnames.
fields.label: Search Accounts

fields.description: Propose a complete numbered chart of accounts for a company from a static template, in the shape import_chart_of_accounts takes. Read-only: it reads the company's existing roots and account numbers so the proposal can flag collisions, and creates nothing.
fields.label: Propose Clean Chart

fields.description: Read-only. The company's cost centers as a nested tree, with numbers, group flags and disabled flags. Cost centers are the axis a posting is filed under alongside the account.
fields.label: List Cost Centers

fields.description:
Every one of these is off on a fresh install and stays off until you tick it. Each call is recorded in MCP Action Log with its arguments and its docstatus change. Enable the narrowest set that does the job: create_journal_entry alone gives an AI a scratchpad in the ledger, because a draft affects no balance until submit_journal_entry — a separate switch — posts it.

Two more write tools live in the sections below: Advance Workflow (Workflow) and Create Todo (Comments & Tasks). The banner at the top of this form always lists every write tool that is currently live, wherever its switch is.
fields.label: Accounting Write Tools

fields.description: Create a DRAFT Journal Entry (docstatus 0). Cannot submit. Balances are unaffected until something else submits it.
fields.label: Create Journal Entry

fields.description: Submit an existing draft Journal Entry (0 to 1). THIS MOVES BALANCES and writes GL Entries.
fields.label: Submit Journal Entry

fields.description: Cancel a submitted Journal Entry (1 to 2), writing reversing GL Entries. Requires a reason.
fields.label: Cancel Journal Entry

fields.description: WRITE. Set or change party_type and party on ONE line of a Journal Entry, including a submitted one, in both the voucher and its GL Entry rows. Moves no balance — account, debit, credit and date are not arguments. Requires a reason, which is written to the entry's comment thread.
fields.label: Update Journal Entry Party

fields.description: Insert a DRAFT Bank Transaction.
fields.label: Create Bank Transaction

fields.description: Attach payment vouchers to a Bank Transaction, up to its unallocated amount.
fields.label: Reconcile Bank Transaction

fields.description: WRITE. Create the Bank Account record a bank feed writes into, and the Bank institution behind it. Refuses a GL account that is not an Asset (a bank account) or a Liability (a credit card), and an Asset account whose account_type is not Bank or Cash — ERPNext's own reconciliation filters on that flag.
fields.label: Create Bank Account

fields.description: WRITE. Book a historical event as a DRAFT opening-balance journal entry, computing the offsetting line against Opening Balance Equity and flagging the entry as opening. Never submits.
fields.label: Set Opening Balance

fields.description: WRITE. Book a whole opening balance sheet as one journal entry — every line explicit, the balancing difference going to an offset account you name. Posts the entry too when asked, which also requires Submit Journal Entry above.
fields.label: Post Opening Balance Journal Entry

fields.description: WRITE. Submit many draft journal entries in one call, each in its own transaction so one failure does not undo the rest. Also requires Submit Journal Entry: that switch is where posting is allowed or not, and this one does not go round it.
fields.label: Bulk Submit Journal Entries

fields.description: WRITE. Delete a DRAFT journal entry outright, recording what it was and why in the audit log. Refuses submitted entries (cancel those instead) and cancelled ones — a cancelled entry and its reversing rows are the audit trail.
fields.label: Delete Draft Journal Entry

fields.description:
Structural changes to the chart itself, as opposed to postings into it. A bad journal entry is one wrong number a reversing entry fixes; a bad reparent silently changes what every balance-sheet subtotal has meant, retroactively, for every period already reported. Enable the narrowest set that does the job.

The read-only planner that produces a chart to review, Propose Clean Chart, is in the Accounting Read Tools section above. Import Chart Of Accounts defaults to a dry run even when it is switched on.
fields.label: Chart of Accounts

fields.description: WRITE. Create one account under an existing group. Validates the parent, the root type, the number's uniqueness and whether the account type can sit under that root before writing anything.
fields.label: Create Account

fields.description: WRITE. Rename, renumber, re-type or re-enable one account. Goes through ERPNext's own update_account_number so the docname moves with the fields. Cannot reparent.
fields.label: Update Account

fields.description: WRITE. Reparent one account. Moves no GL entry, but changes which subtotal every existing posting rolls up into, for every period already reported. The most consequential switch in this section.
fields.label: Move Account

fields.description: WRITE. Soft-delete an account. Requires a reason and refuses any account with GL entries in the current fiscal year. Nothing is deleted and it can be re-enabled.
fields.label: Disable Account

fields.description: WRITE. Build a whole tree of accounts from JSON in one transaction, rolling back entirely on any failure. Defaults to a dry run that creates nothing; a caller has to ask for the real one.
fields.label: Import Chart Of Accounts

fields.description: WRITE, AND IRREVERSIBLE — the only tool here with no undo, no draft and no cancelled state. Hard-deletes an account with no GL entries, no journal entry lines, no children, no company default and no bank account pointing at it. Prefer Disable Account for anything with history; this exists to free an account NUMBER, which disabling does not.
fields.label: Delete Account

fields.description: The calendar the ledger is allowed to post into. ERPNext refuses any posting whose date falls outside a fiscal year, and it refuses it from inside the document being saved — so booking anything historical needs the year to exist first. Creating one books nothing and moves no balance.
fields.label: Fiscal Years

fields.description: WRITE. Create a Fiscal Year so ERPNext will accept postings dated inside it — the prerequisite for booking anything historical. Refuses a name already in use and a date range overlapping another year for the same company.
fields.label: Create Fiscal Year

fields.description: WRITE. Move a fiscal year's dates or enable/disable it. Refuses a move that would leave existing GL entries outside any fiscal year, and cannot rename the year or change which companies it applies to.
fields.label: Update Fiscal Year

fields.description:
How a posting is classified once it reaches an account: which segment of the business it belongs to (cost centers), what other axes it is filed under (accounting dimensions), and which accounts a document reaches for when nothing says (company defaults).

The read-only tree, List Cost Centers, is in the Accounting Read Tools section above. Create Accounting Dimension is the only switch in this app that can add a DocType to your site — and only when a call asks for it explicitly.
fields.label: Cost Centers & Dimensions

fields.description: WRITE. Create one cost center under an existing group. Validates the parent and the number's uniqueness before writing anything. Cannot create a root: ERPNext gives every company exactly one, named after the company.
fields.label: Create Cost Center

fields.description: WRITE. Rename, renumber or disable/enable one cost center. Moves the docname with the fields. Cannot reparent — this app ships no tool that can.
fields.label: Update Cost Center

fields.description: WRITE, AND A SCHEMA CHANGE. Creates an Accounting Dimension and adds a Link custom field to the documents that carry it — and, when the call asks for it, generates the custom DocType whose records become the dimension's values. Those fields are permanent until somebody removes them in the Desk. The narrowest switch in this section to leave off.
fields.label: Create Accounting Dimension

fields.description: WRITE. Add one value to an existing accounting dimension — one record in the DocType that dimension points at. Touches no ledger and creates no fields.
fields.label: Create Dimension Value

fields.description: WRITE. Point the company's default account and cost center fields at real accounts, type-checked (a Receivable field has to name a Receivable account). Changes no existing posting, only what the next document picks by default. Idempotent.
fields.label: Set Company Defaults

fields.description: WRITE. The same fields, but FOUND rather than given — by account number for a numbered chart, then by account type, then by root type, with every candidate passing the same type checks. The setup call to make after Create Company. Never fills a field with something merely plausible: what it cannot resolve it reports. Idempotent.
fields.label: Wire Company Default Accounts

fields.description: Reading a site's approval structure, and — behind its own switch — acting on it. Workflow actions run through Frappe's own apply_workflow, so they respect the acting user's roles and the transition's conditions.
fields.label: Workflow

fields.description: Every Workflow definition: governed DocType, states, transitions and roles.
fields.label: List Workflows

fields.description: Where one document sits in its workflow and which transitions lead out of that state.
fields.label: Get Workflow State

fields.description: Documents parked in a state that still has an action available, optionally narrowed to one user's roles.
fields.label: List Pending Approvals

fields.description: Which workflow actions the acting MCP user can take on a document right now.
fields.label: List Available Actions

fields.description: WRITE. Take a workflow action on a document via Frappe's apply_workflow. Moves state and can submit or cancel the document, exactly as the Desk button does.
fields.label: Advance Workflow

fields.description: A site's saved reports are usually the most trustworthy answer to an accounting question, because somebody who knew the schema already wrote them. run_report enforces the acting user's permission on the report's DocType, so it can reach figures the raw read tools cannot — and is bounded by the roles you gave the MCP System User.
fields.label: Reports

fields.description: Every saved Report, its ref_doctype and its report_type.
fields.label: List Reports

fields.description: Run a Query, Script or Report Builder report and return its rows. Respects the acting user's permission on the report's DocType. Reports often expose figures the individual read tools do not.
fields.label: Run Report

fields.description: The read tools check read permission on the parent document before returning anything, and treat an unattached private file as its owner's. Turn Get Attachment Content off if files on this site hold anything an AI client should never read. Attach File To Document writes, needs write permission on the parent, and is off by default.
fields.label: Attachments

fields.description: Files attached to a document. Checks read permission on that document.
fields.label: List Attachments

fields.description: Base64 content of one attachment, size-capped. Honours private-file permissions. Turn this off if attachments on this site hold anything an AI client should not read.
fields.label: Get Attachment Content

fields.description: WRITE. Attach a file to ANY document — a statement onto the Journal Entry that books it, a receipt onto a Bank Transaction, a contract onto an Asset. Creates one File and changes nothing else. Needs write permission on the parent document, refuses a cancelled parent unless told otherwise, and refuses a filename the document already has.
fields.label: Attach File To Document

fields.description: Putting a document on paper.
fields.label: Printing

fields.description: WRITE. Create or update the Print Format that cuts a printed check out of a Payment Entry, laid out for US laser check stock (three 3.5-inch panels: check, stub, stub). Creates no payment and posts nothing — it decides where the fields land on paper. MICR is preprinted on the stock and is never rendered here. Custom format, so bench migrate never overwrites it.
fields.label: Create Check Print Format

fields.description: Files too big to fit in one tool call, moved onto the site a piece at a time. Pieces are rows in a table, so an upload survives a bench restart; a session idle for 24 hours is swept automatically. Staging alone creates no File — Commit Staged File is the switch that decides whether anything lands.
fields.label: Streaming Uploads

fields.description: READ. Every chunked upload in flight: pieces received, which indexes are missing, bytes staged, and whether it is ready to commit. What you call when an upload died partway and you need to resume rather than re-send.
fields.label: List Staged Uploads

fields.description: WRITE. Stage one piece of a file. Creates no File on its own — the pieces sit in a staging table until Commit Staged File assembles them, and are discarded if it never does. Enabling this without Commit Staged File gives an AI somewhere to put bytes and no way to land them.
fields.label: Stage File Chunk

fields.description: WRITE. Assemble a staged upload into a File — attached to a document, or filed as a new Governance Document. Verifies the caller's own SHA-256 and size against the assembled bytes and refuses on mismatch. This is the switch that decides whether a chunked upload can land anything at all.
fields.label: Commit Staged File

fields.description: WRITE. Throw away a staged upload and its pieces. Destroys half a file nobody has committed; creates and removes no File. Low risk, and the way to free a session id without waiting for the 24-hour sweep.
fields.label: Cancel Staged Upload

fields.description: The human layer: what people said about a document, and what is on somebody's list. List Comments checks read permission on the document. Create Todo writes.
fields.label: Comments & Tasks

fields.description: The comment and activity thread on a document. Checks read permission on that document.
fields.label: List Comments

fields.description: ToDo rows assigned to a user.
fields.label: List Assigned Todos

fields.description: WRITE. Assign a ToDo to a user. Touches no ledger, but it does put an item in somebody's queue and notify them.
fields.label: Create Todo

fields.description: Only usable where the Frappe HR (hrms) app is installed — on a site without it these tools are not advertised at all, whatever these switches say. Employee, attendance and leave data is personal information; enable deliberately.
fields.label: HR

fields.description: Employee records with department, designation and status.
fields.label: List Employees

fields.description: READ. One Employee record with the onboarding state a returning worker arrives with — identity and assignment, the compliance columns, and the live I-9, W-4 and badge records those columns are reconciled against. Nothing in this app writes i9_status or w4_status after the hire, so a completed form fills a column still at its hire-time default; Expired and Requires-Update are never written over.
fields.label: Get Employee

fields.description: Per-employee counts of Present / Absent / Half Day / On Leave over a date range.
fields.label: Get Attendance Summary

fields.description: Remaining leave per type for one employee, computed by HR's own balance function.
fields.label: Get Leave Balance

fields.description: Order books and receivables ageing, from ERPNext's Selling, Buying and Accounts modules.
fields.label: Sales & Purchasing

fields.description: Sales Order headers with totals and delivery progress.
fields.label: List Sales Orders

fields.description: Submitted Sales Invoices still owed, with ageing buckets.
fields.label: Get Outstanding Invoices

fields.description: Purchase Order headers with totals and receipt progress.
fields.label: List Purchase Orders

fields.description: Sprint 3 of the Gap Closure Plan (v0.68.0): create, receive, bill and pay a purchase. Every create tool below produces a DRAFT only (docstatus 0) and cannot submit — posting is the separate, separately-switched submit tool for that same document, so an operator can grant "propose a Purchase Order" without granting "commit the company to buying".
fields.label: Purchasing & AP

fields.description: One Purchase Order in full, including its line items with received_qty and billed_amt.
fields.label: Get Purchase Order

fields.description: One Purchase Receipt in full, including its line items.
fields.label: Get Purchase Receipt

fields.description: Purchase Receipt headers by supplier, status, purchase order, company and date range.
fields.label: List Purchase Receipts

fields.description: One Purchase Invoice in full, including its line items.
fields.label: Get Purchase Invoice

fields.description: Purchase Invoice headers by supplier, status, company, date range and outstanding amount.
fields.label: List Purchase Invoices

fields.description: One Payment Entry in full, including its invoice references.
fields.label: Get Payment Entry

fields.description: Payment Entry headers by supplier, company and date range. Pay/Supplier only — the AP side.
fields.label: List Payment Entries

fields.description: Accounts Payable ageing by supplier, read from GL Entry against every account typed Payable — the true ledger balance, not any one invoice's own column.
fields.label: Get AP Ageing

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a DRAFT Purchase Order against a Supplier. Cannot submit.
fields.label: Create Purchase Order

fields.description: MUTATING. Submit a DRAFT Purchase Order, committing the company to the buy.
fields.label: Submit Purchase Order

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a DRAFT Purchase Receipt against a Supplier. Cannot submit.
fields.label: Create Purchase Receipt

fields.description: MUTATING. Submit a DRAFT Purchase Receipt. On a real site this is what creates the Stock Ledger Entries that move goods into the warehouse.
fields.label: Submit Purchase Receipt

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a DRAFT Purchase Invoice against a Supplier. Cannot submit.
fields.label: Create Purchase Invoice

fields.description: MUTATING. Submit a DRAFT Purchase Invoice, posting GL Entries for the expense and the payable.
fields.label: Submit Purchase Invoice

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a DRAFT Payment Entry paying a Supplier, optionally allocated against submitted Purchase Invoices. Cannot submit.
fields.label: Create Payment Entry

fields.description: MUTATING. Submit a DRAFT Payment Entry, posting GL Entries and reducing every referenced invoice's outstanding amount.
fields.label: Submit Payment Entry

fields.description:
Sprint 5 of the Gap Closure Plan (v0.70.0): the grower-packer money pipeline, from the packer's settlement through revenue, receivables and the cheque.

The chain is Scale Ticket → Settlement Statement → Sales Invoice → Payment Entry. There is deliberately NO Delivery Note: the packer owns the scale, so the scale ticket IS the delivery evidence.

Every create tool below produces a DRAFT only. create_sales_invoice_from_settlement and post_settlement_to_gl are ALTERNATIVES — the first gives proper AR ageing and payment allocation, the second books the same three movements as a journal entry with no subledger. A settlement that has been through one is refused by the other, because two revenue postings for one statement is a double count nobody finds until the year end.
fields.label: Sales, Settlements & AR

fields.description: READ. One Sales Invoice in full: line items, charge rows, every Payment Entry allocated against it, its ageing bucket, and the Settlement Statement it billed.
fields.label: Get Sales Invoice

fields.description: READ. Sales Invoice headers by customer, company, status, settlement and posting date, with the billed and outstanding totals for the rows returned.
fields.label: List Sales Invoices

fields.description: READ. Shrink for one settlement: delivered against packed against culled, with the unexplained remainder reported SEPARATELY from the cull — a cull percentage is what a grower renegotiates a contract over, an unexplained percentage is what a grower asks a question about. Broken down per variety and grade where the tickets and the priced lines can be compared.
fields.label: Get Settlement Shrink

fields.description: READ. Packout across settlements for a period, grouped by variety, grade, customer, field or month. Read `basis` first: for two of the five groupings one side of the ratio genuinely cannot be attributed and is returned as null rather than allocated pro-rata.
fields.label: Get Packout Summary

fields.description: READ. Accounts Receivable ageing grouped by CUSTOMER, cross-checked against GL Entry the way get_ap_aging is. The aggregate companion to get_outstanding_invoices, which lists invoices — both coexist because a collections call and a dashboard want different shapes.
fields.label: Get AR Ageing

fields.description: READ. The whole season in one answer: tickets, settlements, invoices and payments, with the three gaps between them named — fruit delivered that no settlement claimed, settlements nobody invoiced, invoices nobody collected.
fields.label: Get Season Summary

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a DRAFT Sales Invoice, either from hand-written line items or from a submitted Settlement Statement. Cannot submit.
fields.label: Create Sales Invoice

fields.description: MUTATING. One step from a submitted settlement to a DRAFT Sales Invoice: every priced line becomes an invoice line, every deduction a negative charge row, and both link fields are set. Refused on a settlement already invoiced or already posted to the ledger.
fields.label: Create Sales Invoice From Settlement

fields.description: MUTATING. Submit a draft Sales Invoice, which is what recognises the revenue: ERPNext's own controller writes the GL entries and this tool reads them back.
fields.label: Submit Sales Invoice

fields.description: MUTATING. Record money received from a customer as a DRAFT Payment Entry, allocated against named invoices or oldest-first across everything outstanding. Receive/Customer only — it cannot spend money. Submitting it is a separate switch.
fields.label: Receive Payment

fields.description: MUTATING. Book a submitted settlement as a DRAFT Journal Entry instead of a Sales Invoice — receivable and deductions debited, gross revenue credited. The alternative path: it gives no subledger, so the receivable cannot be aged as a document. Stamps the settlement so a second posting through either path is refused.
fields.label: Post Settlement To GL

fields.description: MUTATING. Match late-arriving Scale Tickets to a settlement that already exists, running the same four checks create_settlement_statement runs. Reports how far the variance with the packer moved and in which direction; changes no weight, price or total on the settlement itself.
fields.label: Reconcile Settlement To Tickets

fields.description:
Sprint 4 of the Gap Closure Plan (v0.69.0): what is on hand, how it got there, and when to buy more. Three ERPNext doctypes answer three different questions and are easy to confuse — Stock Entry is the instruction, Stock Ledger Entry is the immutable history, and Bin is the current balance ERPNext maintains from that history.

create_stock_entry produces a DRAFT only, which moves nothing; submit_stock_entry is the separately-switched tool that actually writes the ledger rows and moves every affected balance. Granting the first without the second gives a client a way to propose a movement a human still has to approve in the Desk.
fields.label: Stock & Inventory

fields.description: One Stock Entry in full, with each line's source and target warehouse and where the movement came from.
fields.label: Get Stock Entry

fields.description: Stock Entry headers by type, date range, warehouse and item. The warehouse and item filters are applied against the lines, since neither is a column on the header.
fields.label: List Stock Entries

fields.description: On-hand quantity and value for one item per warehouse, read from Bin. An item with no Bin row has never moved there, which is reported as such rather than as a counted zero.
fields.label: Get Stock Balance

fields.description: Movement history from Stock Ledger Entry: one row per movement with the balance it produced and the voucher that caused it. Cancelled rows excluded.
fields.label: Get Stock Ledger

fields.description: Everything on hand in one warehouse, with each item's reorder rule and a below-reorder flag.
fields.label: Get Warehouse Summary

fields.description: Items below their reorder level, worst shortfall first. An item with a rule and no stock record at all is reported at zero rather than skipped.
fields.label: List Reorder Alerts

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a DRAFT Stock Entry (Material Receipt, Issue or Transfer). Writes no ledger row and moves no balance. Cannot submit.
fields.label: Create Stock Entry

fields.description: MUTATING. Submit a DRAFT Stock Entry. This is the switch that lets a client move stock: ERPNext writes the Stock Ledger Entries and updates every affected Bin, and undoing it is a cancellation rather than an edit.
fields.label: Submit Stock Entry

fields.description: MUTATING. Set the reorder level and quantity for one item in one warehouse. ERPNext keys a reorder rule by warehouse, so both are required.
fields.label: Set Reorder Level

fields.description:
Items, Item Groups, Suppliers, Customers, Warehouses and prices — the records every other ERPNext document points at. None of these doctypes is submittable, so nothing here creates a draft: a master is live the moment it is created, and disabled is the nearest thing to holding one back.

The word company means three different things across these tools, and each one reports which it applied: a Warehouse really is company-scoped, an Item is scoped only through its per-company default row, and a Supplier or Customer is site-wide and has no company column at all.
fields.label: Master Data

fields.description: The Item Group tree, flat, with each node's parent.
fields.label: List Item Groups

fields.description: Create one Item Group under an existing group node.
fields.label: Create Item Group

fields.description: Items by group, stock flag and disabled flag. A company filter here means 'has a default row for this company'.
fields.label: List Items

fields.description: One Item in full, with its per-company defaults and reorder rules.
fields.label: Get Item

fields.description: Create one Item. Live on creation — an Item has no draft state.
fields.label: Create Item

fields.description: Change an Item's description, group, disabled flag, default warehouse or reorder rule. Never renames it.
fields.label: Update Item

fields.description: Suppliers by group and disabled flag. Site-wide: a company filter is reported as not applied.
fields.label: List Suppliers

fields.description: One Supplier in full, with per-company payable-account overrides and linked addresses.

fields.description:
Structured artefacts for somebody who has to sign something off — each carries its own provenance and its own anomaly flags, and an ERROR flag means the numbers do not internally agree. All read-only: nothing is stored, emailed or filed.

The first two switches are the MCP tools; the rest are the individual packet types, each gated separately so you can expose a reconciliation packet without exposing a payroll one.
fields.label: Compliance Packets

fields.description: Which packet types this site can produce, and the filters each takes. Discovery only.
fields.label: List Compliance Packets

fields.description: Build a packet and return it inline. Nothing is stored, emailed or filed. Reads only what the packet needs.
fields.label: Generate Compliance Packet

fields.description: One account, one period: opening and closing balances, every Journal Entry that touched it, the drafts that would change it, the cancellations a balance query cannot see, and a check that the arithmetic closes.
fields.label: Reconciliation Packet

fields.description: A year for an outside CPA: trial balance, income statement, balance sheet, twenty largest entries, intercompany activity, document counts, and a check that the accounting identity holds.
fields.label: Fiscal Year Audit Packet

fields.description: The member register and its event trail. The cap table is the only place on this site that maps an anonymous member id to a legal name — gate it accordingly.
fields.label: Cap Table and Member Events

fields.description: READ. One company's member register: anonymous id, legal entity name, entity type, admission and withdrawal dates, ownership percentage. This is the tool that de-anonymises the ledger, so turning it off is a real choice.
fields.label: List Cap Table

fields.description: WRITE. Register one member: the anonymous id the ledger is tagged with, and the legal entity behind it. Refuses a duplicate member id, and an id that is not already a value of the Member accounting dimension.
fields.label: Create Cap Table Entry

fields.description: WRITE. Change a member's legal name, entity type, admission date, percentage, cost center or notes. Cannot retire a member and cannot change the member id.
fields.label: Update Cap Table Entry

fields.description: WRITE. Retire a member: withdrawal date, retired flag, and a Withdrawal event in the trail. Moves no money — a final distribution is a separate Record Member Event call.
fields.label: Close Cap Table Entry

fields.description: READ. Contributions, distributions, admissions, withdrawals, transfers and reallocations, with the narrative for each and the journal entry that books it.
fields.label: List Member Events

fields.description: WRITE. Record one member event and, where it books money, the DRAFT journal entry for it — tagged with the member dimension on every line. Enabling this grants creating that draft; it does not grant posting it.
fields.label: Record Member Event

fields.description: WRITE. Post the draft journal entry a member event is waiting on. Also requires Submit Journal Entry to be on — that switch is where moving a balance is decided, whatever route reaches it.
fields.label: Submit Member Event

fields.description: WRITE. Record an owner draw / member distribution as a draft Journal Entry — debit an equity draw account, credit bank or cash. Requires the Member Manager role (or System Manager) on top of this switch. Independent of the cap table: works whether or not this site uses Member Event.
fields.label: Create Owner Draw

fields.description: The durable archive: operating agreements, trust documents, resolutions, prior statements, and the amendment chain between them.
fields.label: Governance Documents

fields.description: READ. What is in the archive, with the amendment chain and which entries are still operative.
fields.label: List Governance Documents

fields.description: READ. One archived document's metadata and the bytes of its attachment, base64. Enforces read permission on the document, like the other attachment tools.
fields.label: Read Governance Document

fields.description: WRITE. File a governing document, attach its content as a private file, and chain it onto whatever it supersedes. Refuses a duplicate title and a circular chain.
fields.label: Attach Governance Document

fields.description: WRITE. Convert an entry's .docx attachment to PDF, attach the PDF beside it, and repoint the entry at it — because a .docx is an editing format that renders differently everywhere and some applications will not open at all. The .docx is KEPT. Needs LibreOffice headless in the container and refuses cleanly without it; overwriting an existing PDF is a separate, non-default flag.
fields.label: Regenerate Governance Document PDF

fields.description: Assets that serve more than one part of the business, and assets that are financed. Depreciation written here is split by usage and is always a draft.
fields.label: Assets and Depreciation

fields.description: READ. For every financed asset, whether its remaining depreciation and its note's remaining term still agree, and by how many months they do not.
fields.label: Depreciation / Note Alignment Check

fields.description: WRITE. Create an ERPNext Asset plus the cost profile holding its usage split and schedule. Switches ERPNext's own depreciation OFF on that asset, because this app then owns the schedule and both running would depreciate it twice.
fields.label: Create Asset

fields.description: WRITE. Replace an asset's cost center split. Not retroactive: periods already written keep the split they were written with.
fields.label: Update Asset Allocation

fields.description: WRITE. Tie an asset to the note that financed it, refusing by default unless its useful life equals the note's tenor so paid-off and fully-depreciated fall in the same month.
fields.label: Link Asset to Note

fields.description: WRITE. Write the depreciation due up to a date as draft journal entries, split across each asset's cost centers. Dry run by default; every period written is recorded so it cannot be written twice.
fields.label: Run Depreciation Cycle

fields.description: What the company owes and on what terms. A payment produces a draft journal entry; closing a note posts nothing at all.
fields.label: Notes Payable

fields.description: READ. Every note or loan a company owes: lender, original and outstanding principal, rate, term, and when the next payment falls due.
fields.label: List Notes Payable

fields.description: WRITE. Register an outstanding note: its terms, its provenance, the liability account it posts to, and the asset it financed. Refuses by default when a linked asset's useful life and the note's term disagree.
fields.label: Create Note Payable

fields.description: WRITE. Split a payment into principal and interest and draft the journal entry that books it, decrementing the note's outstanding balance. Never submits.
fields.label: Record Loan Payment

fields.description: WRITE. Close a note as Paid Off, Refinanced or Written Off, recording the disposition in its own history. Writes no journal entry — relieving a written-off balance is a posting with tax consequences that somebody should make on purpose.
fields.label: Close Note Payable

fields.description: The land register and the leases over it. Nothing in this group posts: a lease with rent on it produces no journal entry, and linking a parcel to a Fixed Asset moves no balance.
fields.label: Real Estate

fields.description: READ. One entity's land register with acreage and appraised value totalled, and the oldest and newest appraisal dates.
fields.label: List Parcels

fields.description: READ. One parcel in full, with the leases over it and the Fixed Asset carrying it.
fields.label: Get Parcel

fields.description: WRITE. Register a parcel: county, assessor parcel id, acreage, use type, appraised value and the date it was appraised as of. Refuses a duplicate name or a duplicate assessor id inside one entity.
fields.label: Create Parcel

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered parcel. Cannot re-key it, cannot move it between entities, and cannot set the asset link — that is its own tool.
fields.label: Update Parcel

fields.description: WRITE. Point a parcel at the Fixed Asset carrying it and report the gap between cost and appraised value. Sets one field; posts nothing.
fields.label: Link Parcel to Asset

fields.description: WRITE. Move a Parcel to another Company as a conveyance: the parcel record, its attachments, and every lease, block, irrigation zone, housing unit and housing assignment pointing at it. Writes no Journal Entry — recording a conveyance and booking its consequences are separate acts. Refuses over an active lease.
fields.label: Convey Parcel

fields.description: READ. Leases in both directions with the annual rent roll, and which ones run out soon. Never expires a lease itself.
fields.label: List Leases

fields.description: READ. One lease in full, with the parcel it covers and its attachments.
fields.label: Get Lease

fields.description: WRITE. Record a lease in either direction, with the executed document attached. Books nothing — recording the agreement and booking its consequences are separate acts.
fields.label: Create Lease

fields.description: WRITE. Change a recorded lease's status, term, rent or parties. Refuses to mark one Terminated without a termination date.
fields.label: Update Lease

fields.description: The governance register of who is related to the company and how. Separate from the Party field on a Journal Entry, which is unaffected by anything here.
fields.label: Related Parties

fields.description: READ. The related-party register, current and ended, and which relationships have no governing document behind them.
fields.label: List Related Parties

fields.description: READ. One relationship with everything pointing at it. Never returns more than four digits of a taxpayer id, including from a linked Supplier.
fields.label: Get Related Party

fields.description: WRITE. Register a relationship. Stores the last four digits of a taxpayer id and refuses nine — the full number belongs on the signed W-9, not on this site.
fields.label: Create Related Party

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered relationship. Cannot re-key it: a change of role is a new relationship, and the old entry gets an end date rather than being deleted.
fields.label: Update Related Party

fields.description: Tools that build a document — a PDF report, a tax workbook — and file it in the governance archive with the file attached. They create a Governance Document and Files; they post nothing to the ledger.
fields.label: Generated Documents

fields.description: WRITE. Build the quarter's investment report as a PDF and file it as a Prior Statement. Refuses a quarter that is not genuinely closed — the statement filed, every investment entry submitted, every bank transaction reconciled — and names everything missing in one reply.
fields.label: Generate Quarterly Investment Report

fields.description: WRITE. Aggregate a year of supplier payments into a 1099-NEC workbook and per-recipient forms. A PRE-FILL: taxpayer ids print as the last four digits only, and Copy A is stamped as an information copy rather than a filing.
fields.label: Generate 1099-NEC Pre-Fill

fields.description: READ. Every company with its abbreviation, currency, tax-id status, fiscal year period, cost center and account counts, and the GL entry count with first and last posting dates.
fields.label: List Companies

fields.description: WRITE. Stand up a Company plus its chart of accounts, cost centers and the fiscal year containing today. Refuses a duplicate name or abbreviation, an unknown country or currency, and a non-group parent.
fields.label: Create Company

fields.description: WRITE. Change a company's country, tax id or notes — and its currency only while nothing is posted. Refuses the abbreviation, the name, and the fiscal year start month, each with the reason.
fields.label: Update Company

fields.description: WRITE. Register the Family and Contact Party Types so a Journal Entry line can carry them. Idempotent, and already seeded on install and on every migrate. Changes no existing record.
fields.label: Register Party Types

fields.description: READ. The block register with acreage totalled, plantings summarised, and the varieties already in use on this site.
fields.label: List Fields

fields.description: READ. One block in full, with its irrigation zones, their water rights, and how much of the block is not zoned.
fields.label: Get Field

fields.description: READ. One parcel rolled up: blocks, planted acres against the parcel's own, zones, flow, planting ages, and the food-safety gaps.
fields.label: Parcel Field Summary

fields.description: READ. The zone register with area and flow totalled, plus the zones with no water test and the surface-water zones with no water right.
fields.label: List Irrigation Zones

fields.description: READ. One zone in full, with the block it waters and that block's share of it.
fields.label: Get Irrigation Zone

fields.description: WRITE. Register a planted block under a parcel, with its food-safety facts. Refuses a duplicate name on one parcel, a claimed Farm App id, and blocks summing to more acres than the parcel has.
fields.label: Create Field

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered block. Cannot re-key it, cannot move it to another parcel, and cannot set the cost center — that is its own tool.
fields.label: Update Field

fields.description: WRITE. Point a block at the Cost Center its costs book to. Sets one field; posts nothing and moves no existing entry.
fields.label: Link Field to Cost Center

fields.description: WRITE. Create Fields from a batch of legacy Farm App records carrying their ids. Dry run by default, whole batch validated before the first insert, never updates an existing record.
fields.label: Import Farm App Fields

fields.description: WRITE. Register a zone under a block. Refuses a duplicate zone name on the parcel, a zone number already used on that block, and zones summing to more area than the block.
fields.label: Create Irrigation Zone

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered zone. Cannot re-key it, cannot move it to another block, and cannot set the area in acres — that is computed.
fields.label: Update Irrigation Zone

fields.description: WRITE. Correct one place in any of the four location registers (Field, Irrigation Zone, Parcel, Housing Unit) through one door, taking the doctype/name pair list_farm_locations reports on every row. The register's own update tool does the write, with every refusal it has always made; a column the named register does not have is refused BY NAME rather than dropped. Cannot rename a place and cannot move it to another parent.
fields.label: Update Farm Location

fields.description: WRITE, IRREVERSIBLE. Remove one row from a location register, and ONLY where nothing has ever used it. FOUR CHECKS, every one a refusal: no blocks, zones or cabins registered under it; no record linking to it; no task, spray record, observation or inspection naming it through a DYNAMIC link (the one Frappe's own link integrity does not see); and no file attached to it. The undo for a mis-registration typed ten minutes ago; a place with any history at all is refused, with the count and up to eight examples of what blocks it. dry_run=true runs all four and deletes nothing.
fields.label: Delete Farm Location

fields.description: READ. The camp register with capacity, occupancy and open beds, plus the overdue inspections, the uninhabitable units and the ones filled past what their floor area allows.
fields.label: List Housing Units

fields.description: READ. One unit in full with its whole assignment history, and the compliance gaps named in sentences.
fields.label: Get Housing Unit

fields.description: READ. Who is housed where, currently or over a period, with the wage-deduction assignments named and the deposits still held.
fields.label: List Housing Assignments

fields.description: READ. Beds, bodies and overdue inspections per parcel and in total, with a plain readout.
fields.label: Housing Capacity

fields.description: READ. Everywhere one person has been housed, in order, with deposits and wage deductions.
fields.label: Employee Housing History

fields.description: WRITE. Register a building on a camp with its compliance facts. Computes the lawful occupancy from floor area unless one is given.
fields.label: Create Housing Unit

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered unit. Cannot re-key it and cannot move it between parcels.
fields.label: Update Housing Unit

fields.description: WRITE. Put one person in one unit from a date. Refuses an overlapping assignment unless multi-occupancy is asked for, a non-residential unit, an uninhabitable one, and an unknown employee where an HR app is installed.
fields.label: Create Housing Assignment

fields.description: WRITE. Write the date somebody moved out and the deposit returned. Never deletes: the record is the audit trail for IRS Section 119 and for a wage claim.
fields.label: End Housing Assignment

fields.description: READ. Which blocks a GPS fix is inside. Bounding box first, then exact point-in-polygon; the boundary counts as inside. This is the geofence query.
fields.label: Find Fields Containing a Point

fields.description: READ. Which blocks an H3 cell touches, at any resolution. The spatial-index join for anything else keyed on H3.
fields.label: Find Fields by H3 Cell

fields.description: WRITE. Give a block its GeoJSON polygon and derive centroid, bounding box, H3 coverage and area from it. Refuses invalid or self-intersecting shapes, coordinates off Earth, and an area more than 25% from the recorded acreage.
fields.label: Set Field Boundary

fields.description: WRITE. The same for an irrigation zone, and reports whether it sits inside the block it waters — reported rather than enforced, because a shared line really does cross boundaries.
fields.label: Set Zone Boundary

fields.description: WRITE. The same for a parcel — the OUTER shape, the one the deed and the tax bill both describe — and reports which of the blocks, zones and cabins registered on it fall outside it. Reported rather than enforced: a planting that predates a deed split really does straddle the line. This closes the gap set_field_boundary apologised for on every call from v0.12.0 to v0.31.0, when a parcel had no boundary to check a block against.
fields.label: Set Parcel Boundary

fields.description: WRITE. Set boundaries on existing blocks from a GeoJSON FeatureCollection. Dry run by default, per-feature errors, and it never creates a Field.
fields.label: Import Field Boundaries

fields.description: READ. Everybody a Family-party posting can name, with their relationship and whether a related-party record sits behind them.
fields.label: List Family Members

fields.description: READ. One family member with their related-party record and every posting that names them, read live from the ledger.
fields.label: Get Family Member

fields.description: WRITE. Put one person on the family register so a journal entry line can carry party_type='Family' and name them. Holds no tax id on purpose.
fields.label: Add Family Member

fields.description: WRITE. Change relationship, related party, active flag or notes. Cannot rename — the name is the docname every posting points at.
fields.label: Update Family Member

fields.description: READ. What compliance requires of an operational record on this site, field by field — which framework wants each one, why, and what breaks in the day-to-day WORK if it is missing.
fields.label: Compliance Field Map

fields.description: WRITE, and the ONE switch in this app that defaults ON. Adds the compliance columns — applicator, EPA reg number, REI, PHI, weather, I-9 status, W-4 status, wage-law jurisdiction, traceability links — to Spray Log, Employee and the BucketLog bridge, as Custom Fields, on every migrate. This is the one place erpnext_mcp extends a DocType it did not create, and it is deliberate: compliance woven into the operational record is defensible under audit and a shadow log beside it is not. Turn it OFF and no field is ever added. See docs/compliance_fields.md.
fields.label: Install Compliance Fields

fields.description: READ. Every written procedure, its version, when it took effect and when it is next due for review.
fields.label: List Compliance Policies

fields.description: READ. One procedure in full, with its whole version chain and every audit that cited it.
fields.label: Get Compliance Policy

fields.description: READ. Which SOP categories each audit regime expects and this company has no policy in force for.
fields.label: Get Policy Coverage

fields.description: READ. The certificate and licence register, soonest expiry first, with what has lapsed and what is inside its renewal window.
fields.label: List Certifications

fields.description: READ. One certificate with its full renewal history, including any period it was allowed to lapse.
fields.label: Get Certification

fields.description: READ. What was filed, to whom, when, and what came back — with the ones still awaiting a response called out.
fields.label: List Regulatory Filings

fields.description: READ. One filing with its response and both attached documents.
fields.label: Get Regulatory Filing

fields.description: READ. Every audit and inspection, with open corrective actions counted and the overdue ones named.
fields.label: List Audit Events

fields.description: READ. One audit in full: scope, findings, and every corrective action with its deadline and its closure.
fields.label: Get Audit Event

fields.description: WRITE. Register one written procedure at one version. Refuses a review date before the effective date.
fields.label: Create Compliance Policy

fields.description: WRITE. Change a procedure's version, dates, owner, status or attached document. Cannot re-key it.
fields.label: Update Compliance Policy

fields.description: WRITE. Replace one procedure with another, writing both ends of the chain in one act so a reader following it from either end reaches the same conclusion.
fields.label: Supersede Compliance Policy

fields.description: WRITE. Register one certificate or licence with the date it stops being a defence.
fields.label: Create Certification

fields.description: WRITE. Change a certificate's dates, holder, issuing body, renewal window or status. Moving the expiration forward is refused here — that is a renewal.
fields.label: Update Certification

fields.description: WRITE. Move the expiration date out and record what was actually done to earn it. Records any period the certificate was allowed to lapse rather than hiding it.
fields.label: Renew Certification

fields.description: WRITE. Record something submitted to an agency. Refuses a filing marked Submitted with no submission date.
fields.label: Create Regulatory Filing

fields.description: WRITE. Record the response, the docket number, the attached documents, the status.
fields.label: Update Regulatory Filing

fields.description: WRITE. Record an audit or inspection with its findings and every corrective action it raised.
fields.label: Create Audit Event

fields.description: WRITE. Change the scope, findings, result or report; add, amend and close individual corrective actions.
fields.label: Update Audit Event

fields.description: WRITE. Declare an audit finished. REFUSES while any corrective action is still open — a closure date over an open finding is the most misleading thing this app could record.
fields.label: Close Audit Event

fields.description: READ. What is due and what is late, worst first, grouped by category — read live from the alerts the nightly sweep maintains.
fields.label: Compliance Calendar

fields.description: READ. One Compliance Alert, described exactly as get_compliance_calendar describes it — the single-row twin, for a caller that already has a docname.
fields.label: One Compliance Alert

fields.description: READ. Resolved alerts over alerts raised, as one comparable number, with the split between conditions that cleared themselves and dismissals somebody made by hand.
fields.label: Audit Readiness Score

fields.description: READ. The one screen an owner opens: crews, harvest, compliance, camp, financial KPIs, weather and what is waiting — with a ranked list of what needs attention.
fields.label: Get Owner Dashboard

fields.description: READ. Every alert rule this site can run, with the state that makes each one fire rather than the date.
fields.label: List Compliance Rules

fields.description: WRITE. Run the whole rule set now instead of waiting for tonight. Creates, refreshes and auto-dismisses alerts; touches no operational record. Supports dry_run.
fields.label: Refresh Compliance Alerts

fields.description: WRITE. Hide one alert until a date. Not a dismissal — the condition is still true and it comes back on its own.
fields.label: Snooze Alert

fields.description: WRITE. Take one alert off the calendar, with a mandatory reason. The reason is the only part of the record nobody can reconstruct.
fields.label: Dismiss Alert

fields.description: WRITE. The same dismissal, gated on the alert's own 'May Be Dismissed From The Field' box — which defaults off, so this refuses almost everything until somebody marks an individual alert stale. It is what the Farm Ops app calls; the ungated Dismiss Alert above is the desk-side route.
fields.label: Dismiss a Dismissible Compliance Alert

fields.description: WRITE. Dismiss every alert matching a filter, with one reason for all of them. REQUIRES a dry run first — the whole calendar is one filter away.
fields.label: Dismiss Alerts in Bulk

fields.description: READ. The training register: who was taught what, when, under which regimes, and what has lapsed. Filters by regime the way an audit packet is assembled — 'every NOP record for the last five years', 'every WPS record for 2026' — and reports the FSMA §112.161 elements each record is missing, including the §112.161(b) supervisor review that a GAP-only operation most often lacks.
fields.label: List Trainings

fields.description: READ. One training record in full, with that person's whole training history and the retention period the tags demand — five years where any tag is NOP (7 CFR 205.103(b)(4)), three for OR-OSHA, two for FSMA and WPS. The longest tag governs, with the citation beside the number.
fields.label: Get Training

fields.description: READ. The training compliance MATRIX: every active employee against every curriculum this operation runs, as of a date, each cell current, due soon, expired or MISSING. The register can only report records that exist, so the person with no WPS training at all appears there as no row; here they have a cell, which is the one an inspector finds first.
fields.label: Get Training Compliance Report

fields.description: READ. What a course IS, in the shape a handset renders it: the safety video link, the materials to lay out, how long it runs, how it is delivered, and every PDF attached to it. The read the compliance matrix needed and did not have — a matrix that names six pickers missing WPS and cannot deliver the training has generated a task for somebody else.
fields.label: Get Training Curriculum

fields.description: READ. One group training session in full: the curriculum, the sign-in sheet with each person's badge scan and signature, and what still stands between it and a completion. Every attendee row carries the state that decides whether it becomes a training record, computed in the same place the completion writes from.
fields.label: Get Training Session

fields.description: READ. The session register — what was taught, when, by whom, and which open sessions still hold somebody marked present without a badge scan or a signature. Filtering by employee answers 'which sessions was Ana at', including the one she attended and did not sign, which produced no record and is invisible to the training register.
fields.label: List Training Sessions

fields.description: MUTATING. Files one training event tagged with every audit it answers — one afternoon can satisfy WPS, Oregon's heat rule, FSMA Subpart C and USDA GAP at once, so the record carries a tag list and appears in every packet it earned. Requires the topics actually covered, because a regime tag without them is a claim an inspector will disallow. Writes the §112.161 fields at the time: trainee signature, farm name, and a date-and-time activity stamp.
fields.label: Record Training

fields.description: MUTATING. Records the FSMA §112.161(b) supervisor review on a training record — reviewed, dated and signed by a supervisor within a reasonable time after the record was made. This is the requirement USDA GAP does not ask for and FDA cites even where the training itself was fine. A separate act from recording the training, which is why it is a separate switch. Refuses a self-review, a supervisor from another entity, and a review dated before the training.
fields.label: Sign Training Supervisor Review

fields.description: MUTATING. Puts the content on a curriculum — the safety video link, the materials list, the duration, the delivery method — so a handset can deliver the training a compliance gap names. It does NOT touch what is already filed: every session and every record carries its own copy of what actually happened, taken on the day.
fields.label: Update Training Type

fields.description: MUTATING. Opens one group training event — a curriculum, a day, a place, a trainer. It writes nothing to anybody's file, which is what makes it safe to open a week early or to cancel; only completing it produces training records.
fields.label: Create Training Session

fields.description: MUTATING. Puts one person on a session's sign-in sheet, identified by the badge scanned at the door — through the same resolve_badge path the crew clock uses, so a retired card or a card belonging to somebody who has left is refused before a name reaches a sheet. A badge and a name that disagree are refused.
fields.label: Add Session Attendee

fields.description: MUTATING. Takes one attendee's signature and files the Signing Evidence row that says how they were identified and where. The session is hashed BEFORE the signature is written, so an operation that edits the topics afterwards can be shown to have done it after the crew signed.
fields.label: Sign Session Attendance

fields.description: MUTATING. Turns every provable attendance on a session into its own Employee Training Record, written through record_training so there is one code path on this site that knows what a training record means. Refuses by default when somebody marked present has no badge scan or no signature, and names them.
fields.label: Complete Training Session

fields.description: MUTATING. Draws the sign-in sheet — the course at the top, a line per person with their badge, the moment they were scanned and their own mark on a ruled line. The page an auditor asks to see, and the page seal_signed_document staples its verification appendix onto. An unsigned line is drawn ruled and empty rather than omitted.
fields.label: Render Training Sign-in Sheet

fields.description: Structured Form I-9 workflow — employment eligibility verification with Section 1/2 status tracking, retention dates, audit logging, and USCIS document type lookup. Only usable where the I-9 doctypes exist (run bench migrate after installing v0.27.0).
fields.label: I-9 Compliance

fields.description: Current I-9 compliance configuration: uniformity rule, E-Verify, employer defaults, reminder lead times.
fields.label: Get I-9 Settings

fields.description: Full I-9 record for one employee. Every call is logged to the I-9 Audit Log.
fields.label: Get I-9 Form

fields.description: All I-9 forms with filtering by company and status.
fields.label: List I-9 Forms

fields.description: I-9s awaiting employer verification — Section 1 done, Section 2 not yet.
fields.label: List Pending I-9 Verifications

fields.description: Immutable audit trail for an employee's I-9 form.
fields.label: Get I-9 Audit Log

fields.description: USCIS-accepted documents for I-9 verification by list category.
fields.label: List I-9 Document Types

fields.description: I-9 forms approaching or past retention date, eligible for destruction.
fields.label: Get I-9 Retention Report

fields.description: Employees whose work authorization expires within N days.
fields.label: List Expiring Work Authorizations

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a Draft I-9 Form for an employee.
fields.label: Create I-9 Form

fields.description: MUTATING. Fill Section 1 of a Draft I-9 (employee info). SSN stripped to last 4.
fields.label: Submit I-9 Section 1

fields.description: MUTATING. Correct a transcription error in a Section 1 that is already filed — date of birth, email, phone, SSN last four, and nothing else. The name, address, citizenship status and immigration identifiers are refused by name: those are what the employee swore to above their signature. Requires System Manager, HR Manager or HR User. Logged as section_1_correction and the rendered PDF is redrawn.
fields.label: Patch I-9 Section 1 (corrections)

fields.description: MUTATING. Fill Section 2 of an I-9 (employer verification). Validates the 3-business-day rule.
fields.label: Submit I-9 Section 2

fields.description: MUTATING. Update I-9 site configuration.
fields.label: Update I-9 Settings

fields.description: MUTATING. Flag a Complete I-9 for reverification when work auth expires.
fields.label: Flag I-9 Reverification

fields.description: MUTATING. Record a Section 3 entry (Form I-9 Supplement B) on an existing I-9 — reverification, rehire, or the document a receipt stood in for. Appends; never overwrites Section 2.
fields.label: Reverify I-9 (Section 3)

fields.description: MUTATING. Mark an I-9 as Destroyed after retention period. Refused if retention date not yet reached.
fields.label: Destroy I-9

fields.description: WRITE. Fill the official USCIS Form I-9 from a record and attach the PDF privately to generated_pdf. Signature boxes are left empty; the SSN box needs include_full_ssn and store_full_ssn.
fields.label: Render I-9 PDF

fields.description: WRITE. File an already-uploaded signed or scanned I-9 against its record as the official signed copy, and make the File private.
fields.label: Attach Signed I-9

fields.description: WRITE. Attach a signature capture to the I-9 or W-4 box a missing-signature alert found empty, close the Farm Task that asked for it, and bring the rendered PDF back into step. The list of signable boxes is closed, the two EMPLOYER boxes still require the authorized-signer roster, and an existing signature is never replaced without overwrite.
fields.label: Collect Form Signature

fields.description: READ. Signature events with the identity check behind each one — who signed, in what capacity, which badge was scanned, on what device, where, and against what hash of the record they were shown. Filter by document, signer, badge, capacity, company or date range. `unverified_count` reports how many of them were captured without an identity check or without a document hash.
fields.label: List Signing Evidence

fields.description: READ. One signature event in full, with the document hash RE-CHECKED against the record as it stands now — `tamper_check.matches` is false where something the signer attested to has been altered since. Also reports whether this attestation was later superseded.
fields.label: Get Signing Evidence

fields.description: READ. The rendered federal form as BYTES, so the person about to sign it can be shown it first — step 1 of the signing evidence chain, and the step the iOS app could not take because both renderers answer with a private file_url the handset cannot follow. It takes no signature, writes no signature column and does not touch the evidence register; it will DRAW the page once where the record has none, which on a fresh I-9 is every time.
fields.label: Get Document Preview

fields.description: MUTATING. Seal a form that has ALREADY been signed: redraw it with every capture stamped into the page content and the AcroForm flattened away, append a verification page naming the signer, the identity check, the moment, the device, the coordinates and the document fingerprint, then hash the finished file and record that hash on every Signing Evidence row for it. An unsigned form is refused — an appendix that vouches for nothing is worse than no appendix. submit_form_signature takes this step automatically, so this tool is for a form signed before v0.63.0 or one whose second signature came through the Desk.
fields.label: Seal Signed Document

fields.description: READ. Who this employer has authorised to sign a federal employment form, and whether the roster is configured at all. AN EMPTY ROSTER MEANS UNRESTRICTED — which is what every site is until somebody adds the first signer, and is why this switch is on by default: a caller has to be able to find out which case a site is in.
fields.label: List Authorized Signers

fields.description: MUTATING. Authorize one User account to sign Form I-9 Section 2 and/or Form W-4's employer block. THE FIRST ROW TURNS ENFORCEMENT ON for the whole site — from then on an account not on the roster cannot complete a Section 2, so add everybody who verifies documents, including yourself.
fields.label: Add Authorized Signer

fields.description: MUTATING. Change one signer's printed name, title, which of the two forms they may sign, or whether the authorisation is live. active=true is how somebody deactivated is put back.
fields.label: Update Authorized Signer

fields.description: MUTATING. Deactivate one authorized signer. The row is KEPT and its active flag cleared — a form signed in a prior season was signed by whoever was authorised then, and a deleted row makes that unanswerable. There is no delete tool.
fields.label: Remove Authorized Signer

fields.description: READ. Retrieve a single W-4 Form by name or employee+tax_year.
fields.label: Get W-4

fields.description: READ. List W-4 Forms with optional filters on employee, company, tax_year, status.
fields.label: List W-4 Forms

fields.description: READ. Return the current FICA Configuration (SS/Medicare/FUTA rates and thresholds).
fields.label: Get FICA Config

fields.description: READ. Return Federal Tax Table brackets for a given tax_year, filing_status, payroll_period.
fields.label: Get Federal Tax Table

fields.description: READ. Preview federal withholding for hypothetical inputs without saving anything.
fields.label: Preview Federal Withholding

fields.description: READ. List active employees who have no current-year W-4 on file.
fields.label: List Employees Missing W-4

fields.description: READ. Calculate full payroll taxes (federal income tax, SS, Medicare, FUTA) for an employee's pay period using their active W-4.
fields.label: Calculate Payroll Taxes

fields.description: MUTATING. Submit a new W-4 Form. If the employee already has an Active W-4 for the same tax year, the old one is set to Superseded.
fields.label: Submit W-4

fields.description: MUTATING. Update FICA Configuration rates and thresholds (SS rate, wage base, Medicare rate, FUTA rate, etc.).
fields.label: Update FICA Config

fields.description: MUTATING. Import or replace Federal Tax Table brackets for a given tax year.
fields.label: Import Federal Tax Table

fields.description: WRITE. Fill the official IRS Form W-4 from a record and attach the PDF privately to generated_pdf. The Employers Only block — name and address, first date of employment, EIN — is resolved from I-9 Settings, the Company and Employee.date_of_joining, so no caller supplies it. The signature line and the SSN box are left for a pen.
fields.label: Render W-4 PDF

fields.description: READ. Retrieve a State Tax Configuration by name or company+state+tax_year.
fields.label: Get State Tax Config

fields.description: READ. List State Tax Configurations with optional filters.
fields.label: List State Tax Configs

fields.description: READ. Return State Tax Table brackets for a given state, tax_year, filing_status.
fields.label: Get State Tax Table

fields.description: READ. Preview state withholding for hypothetical inputs without saving anything.
fields.label: Preview State Withholding

fields.description: READ. Preview combined federal + state payroll taxes for an employee's pay period.
fields.label: Preview Total Payroll Taxes

fields.description: READ. List employees grouped by their most recent work_state from Farm Shift data.
fields.label: List Employees by Work State

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a State Tax Configuration for a company, state, and tax year.
fields.label: Create State Tax Config

fields.description: MUTATING. Update an existing State Tax Configuration's rates and thresholds.
fields.label: Update State Tax Config

fields.description: MUTATING. Import or replace State Tax Table brackets for a given state and tax year.
fields.label: Import State Tax Table

fields.description: READ. Get the active salary structure for an employee — pay type, base rate, effective dates.
fields.label: Get Salary Structure

fields.description: READ. List salary structures with optional filters by company, employee, pay type, active status.
fields.label: List Salary Structures

fields.description: READ. Dry-run payroll calculation for one employee over a date range. Shows gross, deductions, net without creating records.
fields.label: Preview Payroll

fields.description: READ. Get a Farm Payroll Entry with all its payroll slips — totals, per-employee breakdowns, deduction details.
fields.label: Get Payroll Entry

fields.description: READ. List payroll entries with optional filters by company, status, pay frequency.
fields.label: List Payroll Entries

fields.description: READ. One employee's hours in a date range as payroll reads them — their own span on each shift rather than the crew's, overtime resolved week by week at the 40-hour agricultural threshold, hours split by work state, and piece units from whichever source this site records them in. No money, and nothing written.
fields.label: Employee Timesheet Summary

fields.description: READ. Dry-run a whole company's payroll for a pay period off Farm Shift hours. Identical arithmetic to Run Payroll For Period with nothing written, including the three lists to read before the totals: workers with no salary structure, states below their minimum wage, and shifts with no end time.
fields.label: Preview Payroll For Period

fields.description: READ. The payroll register for a period: one row per employee with gross, federal and state withholding, Social Security, Medicare, other deductions, net, hours and piece units, a totals row, and the employer taxes beside them. Recomputes nothing — every figure is read off stored payroll slips, and the runs it added up are named so a disagreement with the bank or the ledger can be traced to one.
fields.label: Payroll Register

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a salary structure for an employee — pay type, base rate, effective period.
fields.label: Create Salary Structure

fields.description: MUTATING. Soft-deactivate a salary structure. Sets is_active to 0 and effective_to to today.
fields.label: Deactivate Salary Structure

fields.description: MUTATING. Generate a full payroll entry for a pay period — creates a Draft entry with calculated slips for every active employee with a salary structure.
fields.label: Calculate Payroll

fields.description: MUTATING. Move a payroll entry from Calculated to Submitted (final).
fields.label: Submit Payroll

fields.description: MUTATING. Compute a whole company's payroll from Farm Shift hours and store it as a Farm Payroll Entry in Calculated status. Overtime is resolved per workweek at 40 hours and wages are split by work state. Reports minimum wage shortfalls, unclosed shifts and workers with no salary structure rather than refusing over them; submitting is a separate switch.
fields.label: Run Payroll For Period

fields.description: MUTATING. Draw one employee's pay stub for one payroll run — earnings itemised, every deduction, net pay, year to date, optionally the employer's own contributions — and attach the PDF privately to the payroll entry. Recomputes nothing and moves no status. Unlike the tax form pages this is not a working copy: it is the itemised statement of earnings an employer is required to give a worker, drawn from the slip that was actually paid.
fields.label: Render Pay Stub

fields.description: READ. The register of garnishments and voluntary deductions, filtered by employee, type, category, status or reference, each row carrying the priority, pre-tax and FICA treatment the payroll engine will actually apply.
fields.label: List Payroll Deductions

fields.description: READ. One deduction in full, with the derived facts that decide the money and the warnings worth reading about it.
fields.label: Get Payroll Deduction

fields.description: READ. Everything standing against one worker's pay, in the order it comes out. Given a gross_pay it prices each line against the CCPA ceilings and reports what would be withheld and what would fall short.
fields.label: List Employee Deductions

fields.description: WRITE. File a garnishment, support order, levy or voluntary election against a worker's pay. Refuses a duplicate active order with the same reference, a garnishment marked pre-tax, and a percentage over 100.
fields.label: Create Payroll Deduction
