fields.description: WRITE. Change a filed deduction, or retire it by setting its status to Suspended or Completed. Cannot move it to another employee or company.
fields.label: Update Payroll Deduction

fields.description: READ. The file of court orders and agency notices this employer has been served with, ranked as federal law ranks them: child support 1, tax levy 2, student loan 3, creditor 4. Names the workers carrying two or more live orders, which is where the shared 25% pool bites.
fields.label: List Garnishments

fields.description: READ. One order in full, with the derived facts and what else competes with it against the same wages. Warns about a stated ceiling above the statutory maximum, an order that can never be satisfied by arithmetic, and an order with no linked deduction, under which nothing is being withheld.
fields.label: Get Garnishment

fields.description: WRITE. File a court order against a worker's wages AND create the payroll deduction that honours it, in one act. This switch governs both halves: an order that withheld nothing would be a garnishment the payroll run cannot see. OFF by default.
fields.label: Create Garnishment

fields.description: WRITE. Change a filed order, post what payroll withheld against its balance, or retire it as Satisfied or Terminated — which also retires the linked deduction, so the withholding actually stops. OFF by default.
fields.label: Update Garnishment

fields.description: WRITE. Draw the employer's acknowledgment back to the issuing court or agency and attach the PDF privately to the order. The employer's own letter — it accompanies any answer form the issuer prescribes and does not replace it. OFF by default.
fields.label: Render Garnishment Response

fields.description: READ. Every handset enrolled for push notifications and whether it is still worth sending to, with the site's own APNs configuration beside the rows — because a bench with no signing key has a perfect register and sends nothing at all.
fields.label: List Push Tokens

fields.description: WRITE. Send one break-tone notification to every handset a worker has enrolled, to prove the pipeline before a real break depends on it. Mutating because it makes a phone in somebody's pocket ring at the time-sensitive interruption level, which rings through Focus.
fields.label: Send Test Push

fields.description: READ. Which general ledger accounts a company's payroll posts to, which of the eleven payroll components are still unmapped, and what each component is for.
fields.label: Get Payroll Account Mapping

fields.description: READ. What the Journal Entries for a payroll run would be — every line, every account, both totals and the balance check — with nothing written. It refuses nothing: an incomplete account mapping or a run already posted is reported as a blocker rather than raised, because an unpostable run is exactly what somebody calls a preview to find out about.
fields.label: Preview Payroll GL

fields.description: MUTATING. Sets which general ledger accounts a company's payroll posts to, one row per payroll component, merging into what is already there unless replace=true. No account name ships as a default: one that is right on this chart of accounts would be quietly wrong on the next farm's. Group accounts are refused when the mapping is written rather than when it is posted from.
fields.label: Configure Payroll Accounts

fields.description: MUTATING. Turns a Farm Payroll Entry into DRAFT Journal Entries — gross pay debited to the wage expense, every withheld amount and the net credited to their liabilities, and the employer's own taxes booked as expense and liability both. It NEVER submits. Refuses a run that is not Calculated or Submitted, a company with no account mapping or an incomplete one, a run that already has live journal entries against it, and any entry that does not balance.
fields.label: Post Payroll To GL

fields.description: READ. What the operation pays for one unit of one piecework activity, and which of those rows is in force. `in_force` is the ONE row per (company, activity) a payroll run dated `on_date` would read; everything else is history, and it is kept because a period already paid must still be explicable.
fields.label: List Piecework Rates

fields.description: READ. One piecework rate in full, and whether it is the row payroll would actually read on a given date — where it is not, the row that covers that date instead is named.
fields.label: Get Piecework Rate

fields.description: READ. The default hourly rate for each job title at each company, and which row a salary structure created on a given date would be seeded from. It says nothing about what any EXISTING structure pays: the default is read once, at creation.
fields.label: List Position Wage Defaults

fields.description: READ. One position wage default in full, and whether it is the row a new hire in that job would start on.
fields.label: Get Position Wage Default

fields.description: MUTATING. Sets what one unit of one piecework activity pays at one company, from one date. THIS IS ALSO HOW A RAISE IS MADE — a row with a later effective_from supersedes the open-ended one from that date on and leaves it paying the periods it already paid. Every worker whose salary structure has base_rate 0 and that activity is paid from it on the next run; a structure naming its own rate is unaffected.
fields.label: Create Piecework Rate

fields.description: MUTATING. Corrects a piecework rate that was typed wrong, or retires it with is_active=false. Moving the rate on a row already in force changes what a re-run over that period computes, and the result says so. company and activity cannot be changed, and there is no delete: a rate that paid a period is the record of what that period paid.
fields.label: Update Piecework Rate

fields.description: MUTATING. Sets the default hourly rate for one job title at one company, from one date. IT SEEDS AND DOES NOT GOVERN: create_salary_structure copies the number onto a new structure once, and structures that already exist are untouched by anything written here.
fields.label: Create Position Wage Default

fields.description: MUTATING. Edits a position wage default or retires it with is_active=false. Salary structures already seeded from it are unchanged, whatever is edited here — an hourly wage is what a person was hired at, and a table that could restate it retroactively would rewrite what a wage claim asks about.
fields.label: Update Position Wage Default

fields.description: READ. List generated tax forms with filters by type, year, quarter, employee and status.
fields.label: List Tax Forms

fields.description: READ. Get one tax form with every computed box and line value as it was calculated at generation time.
fields.label: Get Tax Form

fields.description: MUTATING. Compute a W-2, 1099-NEC, 941, OR-WR, OQ or WA-ESD from the payroll already in the system and record it as a Tax Form. Files nothing.
fields.label: Generate Tax Form

fields.description: MUTATING. Recompute an existing tax form from current payroll data and report which values moved. Refuses a Filed form unless allow_filed is passed.
fields.label: Regenerate Tax Form

fields.description: MUTATING. Record that a form was filed with the agency — status, filing date and confirmation number. Transmits nothing.
fields.label: Mark Tax Form Filed

fields.description: MUTATING. Draw a Tax Form's stored values on the face of the form and attach the PDF to the record. Recomputes nothing, moves no status, and every page is stamped a working copy — it is not a filing and not an official scannable form.
fields.label: Render Tax Form PDF

fields.description: MUTATING. Render PDFs for a set of Tax Forms at once — every W-2 for a year, say. Skips forms that already have one unless overwrite is passed, and refuses a selection larger than the limit rather than truncating it.
fields.label: Bulk Render Tax Form PDFs

fields.description: READ. Everything owed to every tax authority for a period — federal EFTPS, Oregon and Washington — broken down by pay period.
fields.label: Tax Remittance Summary

fields.description: READ. Form 941's lines 1 to 15 for a quarter, plus Part 2's monthly liabilities. Computed from current payroll and recorded nowhere.
fields.label: Form 941 Prefill

fields.description: READ. Oregon's OQ and Form 132, and Washington's ESD quarterly report, with the per-employee detail each state requires.
fields.label: State Tax Remittance

fields.description: READ. Every federal deposit deadline in a period under this employer's monthly or semiweekly schedule, plus the state filing dates.
fields.label: Tax Deposit Schedule

fields.description: READ. Form 940 for a calendar year, with the $7,000 wage base consumed per employee in date order and both agricultural coverage tests.
fields.label: FUTA Summary

fields.description: READ. List expense receipts with filters by status, employee, company, category, task and receipt date range. Lowest OCR confidence first.
fields.label: List Expense Receipts

fields.description: READ. One expense receipt in full — extracted fields, photograph, line items, the raw OCR text behind them, and the review trail.
fields.label: Get Expense Receipt

fields.description: READ. Expense receipts totalled by category and by period (week/month/quarter), optionally broken down by merchant or supplier. Rejected receipts are excluded from the totals by default.
fields.label: Get Expense Summary

fields.description: READ. Every expense receipt in a window, one row each, with an optional CSV export string. Nothing is excluded by default.
fields.label: Get Expense Report

fields.description: MUTATING. Capture an operational expense from a photographed receipt — the OCR-extracted merchant, amount and date, with the image and raw text kept beside them.
fields.label: Submit Expense Receipt

fields.description: MUTATING. Approve an expense receipt, recording which Employee approved it and when. Separate from rejection on purpose: approving and refusing are different permissions.
fields.label: Approve Expense Receipt

fields.description: MUTATING. Reject an expense receipt with a required reason, recording which Employee rejected it and when.
fields.label: Reject Expense Receipt

fields.description: MUTATING. Correct cost_center, supplier, category or notes on a receipt already captured, in any status. Never touches merchant, amount, receipt_date or the review trail.
fields.label: Update Expense Receipt

fields.description: READ. Scale tickets by customer, company, status, variety, field and delivery date. `unmatched: true` answers the question the register exists for — which delivered loads no settlement has claimed yet. Reports a per-unit count beside the summed weight, because kilos and bins do not add.
fields.label: List Scale Tickets

fields.description: READ. One scale ticket in full — the three weights with the subtraction shown, the origin and destination, the photograph of the slip, and the settlement that claimed it.
fields.label: Get Scale Ticket

fields.description: READ. Packer settlement statements by customer, company, status and date, with each one's packout percentage, deductions and net proceeds.
fields.label: List Settlement Statements

fields.description: READ. One settlement in full — priced lines, deductions, computed percentages, and the reconciliation between the packer's delivered weight and the grower's own matched scale tickets. The variance is reported, never corrected.
fields.label: Get Settlement Statement

fields.description: READ. Which register a photographed document belongs in — expense, scale ticket, settlement or bill — from a keyword table that ships in the source, with the matched keywords returned so the answer can be argued with. Touches no doctype at all.
fields.label: Classify Receipt

fields.description: READ. The best-matching Supplier for a merchant string, and how confident that is — plain string similarity, no ML. Suggests a link; never sets one.
fields.label: Normalize Merchant

fields.description: READ. Merchant strings already linked to a Supplier, grouped by which Supplier. Built by reading Expense Receipt rows, not a table of its own.
fields.label: List Merchant Aliases

fields.description: MUTATING. Capture one scale ticket as a DRAFT. Net weight is computed from gross minus tare and cannot be passed; a tare above the gross is refused rather than producing a negative net.
fields.label: Create Scale Ticket

fields.description: MUTATING. Submit a draft scale ticket, which makes it immutable. Separate from capture on purpose: freezing a third party's weight record is not the same permission as writing one down.
fields.label: Submit Scale Ticket

fields.description: MUTATING. Capture one packer settlement statement as a DRAFT, with its priced lines and its deductions. Every percentage and every total is computed here rather than accepted from the statement.
fields.label: Create Settlement Statement

fields.description: MUTATING. Submit a draft settlement statement, which makes it immutable. It posts nothing to the ledger — the tool that books settlement proceeds is a later release.
fields.label: Submit Settlement Statement

fields.description: MUTATING. Turn one Approved Expense Receipt into a draft Purchase Invoice — resolving or creating the Supplier, matching the expense account from the category, and linking the two documents. Refuses an Owner Draw receipt by name.
fields.label: Create Purchase Invoice From Receipt

fields.description: READ. The shift register: who was where, with which crew, for how long, and what is still open. `status` is computed from whether a shift has an end time rather than read off a stored column, because an OPEN shift is what the weather sweep walks. Reports every shift closed WITHOUT a supervisor signature — end_shift cannot produce one, so anything on that list was closed in the Desk, and FSMA §112.161(b) asks for a review dated and signed.
fields.label: List Shifts

fields.description: READ. One shift in full: the crew with each person's own joined_at and left_at, the compliance-event timeline, the weather timeline, and the heat record if one exists. This is the evidence chain an inspector is handed when they ask an operation to prove one shift complied.
fields.label: Get Shift

fields.description: READ. Where the crew went during one shift, in the order the fixes were TAKEN rather than the order they arrived — a phone out of signal posts an hour of breadcrumbs the moment the bars come back, and a track sorted by insertion draws the crew teleporting. Reports every silence longer than ten minutes as a gap and interpolates nothing: an invented position on a record read in a wage dispute is the worst thing this app could put on a map. ON by default, because reading a track cannot create one.
fields.label: Get Shift Track

fields.description: READ. Every documented hot shift and what each one claims about OAR 437-004-1131 — water, shade, rest cycle, observation, training. Reports the shifts where heat illness signs were observed, which is what an investigation reads first, and the ones that do not confirm current heat training, which is a citation on the first hot morning.
fields.label: List Heat Exposure Events

fields.description: READ. One heat record in full with the shift behind it, and the obligations the record does NOT claim were met, in the rule's own terms. Says so when the shift's event timeline is empty — the checkboxes are the assertion and the logged water breaks are the evidence for it.
fields.label: Get Heat Exposure Event

fields.description: MUTATING. Forms a crew at a place and starts the exposure period every compliance question about it is asked against. THE FOREMAN FORMS THE CREW — there is no worker clock-in, because OAR 437-004-1131 puts the water, shade and observation obligations on a named responsible person and a crew of thirty each clocking themselves in is a shift with nobody responsible for the record. Per-worker attendance survives inside the crew envelope as joined_at and left_at on each row.
fields.label: Start Shift

fields.description: MUTATING. Rosters a late arrival or a transfer onto a shift already running. joined_at defaults to NOW rather than to the shift's start, which is the opposite of start_shift's default and right for the same reason — their Attendance record spans from when they actually arrived. Refuses a second row for somebody already on the crew, which would become two payroll days for one person.
fields.label: Add Worker to Shift

fields.description: MUTATING. Ends one worker's time on a shift that continues without them. It SETS left_at and does not delete the row — the row is the only record that this person was on this shift at all, which is what a wage claim turns on and what says who was exposed before they were sent home.
fields.label: Remove Worker from Shift

fields.description: MUTATING. Records one thing the foreman did about the conditions, at the moment it happened — water break, shade break, rest cycle, supervisor observation, cool-down. THE TIMELINE IS THE EVIDENCE: Oregon's heat rule does not ask whether water was available in principle, it asks what happened during the shift, and a timeline written from memory in the evening is what an investigator discounts.
fields.label: Log Shift Event

fields.description: MUTATING. Closes a shift with the supervisor's signature and writes one Attendance record per crew member, each spanning that person's OWN joined_at to their own left_at. The signature is required: an unsigned close is an update statement setting a timestamp, and §112.161(b) asks for a review dated AND signed. The Attendance bridge never blocks the close — a site without Frappe HR or an archived employee is reported, not refused.
fields.label: End Shift

fields.description: MUTATING. Calls a shift off: it was formed and then not worked. Sets `cancelled`, records why, and stamps an end time so the shift stops being Active. IT IS NOT A CLOSE AND WRITES NO ATTENDANCE — `end_shift` says the crew worked and pays them for it; this says they did not. Where the crew worked part of the day before being sent home, end_shift at the hour they stopped is the right tool, and choosing between the two is choosing between 'they were paid for this' and 'they were not'. The crew rows and the event timeline are kept either way. OFF by default like every other write on this form.
fields.label: Cancel Shift

fields.description: MUTATING. Start a break on a shift — rest, meal or cool-down. A thin wrapper over log_shift_event that validates the break-specific fields together. A Crew break covers everybody on the shift; an Individual break must name the employee.
fields.label: Log Shift Break

fields.description: MUTATING. End a running break — write the observed duration. Writes ended_at and the true duration_minutes, and flips duration_source to Observed.
fields.label: End Shift Break

fields.description: READ. The break schedule for a state — the rest, meal and heat cool-down obligations the handset's break coach counts from. Returns the policy with its schedule rows. ON by default because reading a policy cannot create one.
fields.label: Get Break Policy

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a Labor Break Policy — the break schedule for one state in one effective period. A policy is a STATE's rule, not a company's. OFF by default: writing a break schedule is a compliance decision an operator should take on purpose.
fields.label: Create Break Policy

fields.description: MUTATING. Update an existing Labor Break Policy: toggle enabled, change dates, add or replace schedule rows. Schedule tables are replaced wholesale — there is no append mode. OFF by default.
fields.label: Update Break Policy

fields.description: READ. Per-worker bucket counts for a shift, sorted by count descending. The production board: each worker's accepted and rejected bucket counts, hours present, and break reconciliation. ON by default because reading production cannot change it.
fields.label: Get Shift Production

fields.description: READ. Every crew member's OWN envelope on one shift: their span, the weather they personally stood in, the water/shade/rest events inside it, and what their own hours entitle them to. The shift is one record and the crew is not one person — a picker who joined at 09:40 was absent for the hour it was hottest, and a heat record scoped to the crew says otherwise. ON by default because reading an envelope cannot change it.
fields.label: Get Shift Crew Timeline

fields.description: MUTATING. Appends one GPS fix to a shift's track — what the iOS app posts periodically while a shift is running. IT APPENDS AND NEVER EDITS: a breadcrumb somebody can correct is not a record of where the phone was. This is the one tool on the shift surface a worker's phone drives rather than the foreman, and it does not contradict the sole-actor rule — that rule is about who is ANSWERABLE, and a breadcrumb attests to nothing. OFF by default: a location track is a record of where people were, and turning it on is a decision an operator should take on purpose.
fields.label: Log Shift Location

fields.description: MUTATING. Documents OAR 437-004-1131 for one shift, signed and submitted — the answer to 'prove the July 15 crew complied'. At most one per shift, because two records about one exposure period will disagree. Checks the training claim against the register AS OF THE DAY OF THE SHIFT and refuses a verified claim the register contradicts; refuses signs observed with no response and no explanation. Everything else is recorded with the gap stated.
fields.label: Create Heat Exposure Event

fields.description: READ. One shift's conditions across its exposure period, with the extremes and the instant it first reached threshold — the answer to 'how hot was it when the break was called' without reading the whole shift. Says where each reading came from, and calls out a timeline that mixes live fifteen-minute readings with an hourly archive reconstruction, because the two are not equally strong evidence.
fields.label: Get Weather Timeline

fields.description: READ. Closed shifts carrying fewer than one weather reading per hour of their own length — the worklist for the backfill. Shifts with no farm_location_gps are listed separately, because no amount of backfilling documents one and the fix is a different action.
fields.label: List Shifts Missing Weather

fields.description: READ. What this site fetches, how often, the three thresholds a reading is read against and the per-company overrides — because 'the threshold is 80' is false on a site where one entity set 75. There is deliberately NO write counterpart: those are outbound URLs and the numbers that decide whether a hot afternoon gets logged at all, and an operator edits them in the Desk.
fields.label: Get Weather Settings

fields.description: MUTATING. Appends one Open-Meteo reading to an OPEN shift immediately, bypassing the cache — for the foreman who wants the conditions on the record now rather than in eleven minutes. Logs a Threshold Crossed compliance event where the reading crosses, ONCE PER SHIFT rather than once per reading. It never creates a Heat Exposure Event: which crew was exposed and whether the rest cycle was taken are judgements by the person who was there.
fields.label: Fetch Weather Now

fields.description: MUTATING. Reconstructs a CLOSED shift's timeline from Open-Meteo's historical archive, at the archive's own hourly granularity, so a shift that ran before the service was switched on can still be documented. Idempotent — every reading is matched against the minute already present, and a reading is never edited. It writes no compliance events: a Threshold Crossed row dated last July on a signed shift would be an observation nobody made.
fields.label: Backfill Weather for a Shift

fields.description: WRITE. Assemble every piece of evidence for one audit type over one period into a PDF, and file it as a Governance Document. REFUSES an incomplete period — a packet produced while corrective actions are still open would be contradicted by the auditor's first question.
fields.label: Generate Audit Packet

fields.description: READ. Which audit types this site can assemble a packet for, and what each one pulls in.
fields.label: List Audit Packet Types

fields.description: READ, DIAGNOSTIC. Every submitted Journal Entry whose voucher and general ledger disagree about who a line belongs to — the damage class v0.13.0's broken update_journal_entry_party left behind. Writes nothing.
fields.label: Find Drifted JE Attributions

fields.description: WRITE. Walk a list from find_drifted_je_attributions and bring each drifted GL Entry row back into step with its voucher. Moves no balance: party is an attribution column. Supports dry_run.
fields.label: Repair Drifted JE Attributions

fields.description: READ. The pool: every task a worker could pick up right now, with their concurrent-claim count. Self-pick and Either only — dispatched work is not in the pool by design.
fields.label: List Available Tasks

fields.description: READ. What one worker is holding, and their history on request.
fields.label: List Dispatched Tasks

fields.description: READ. The Kanban as JSON: every task grouped by state, with the open Critical work and how much of the board came from a compliance alert.
fields.label: Dispatch Board

fields.description: READ. One task in full — its evidence contract, every assignment and rejection, the record its completion produced, and whether the alert it came from has since auto-dismissed.
fields.label: Get Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. Raise one piece of work. REFUSES without an evidence contract saying what closing it requires, and refuses a creates_record naming a DocType this site does not have.
fields.label: Create Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. A worker in the field reports a problem on the spot. Photo required, rate-limited to 5 per worker per hour. Critical urgency restricted to Foreman and Farm Manager roles.
fields.label: Report Field Task

fields.description: WRITE. Report a problem on a specific asset. Convenience wrapper that auto-fills skill_required from the asset type and creates a linked Farm Task.
fields.label: Report Asset Issue

fields.description: WRITE. Send a named person to a task. Taking work off somebody who already holds it needs reassign=true and a reason, written onto their assignment.
fields.label: Assign Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. A worker takes a task from the pool. Capped at three concurrent claims per worker — a hoarding limit, not a productivity one. Refuses Dispatched work.
fields.label: Claim Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. Clock in on a claimed task. This is the clock-in for the TASK, not the shift, and starting twice is refused.
fields.label: Start Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. Finish a task, check the evidence against its contract, and write the compliance record it promised. REFUSES a submission short of the contract, and refuses a completion filed by anybody other than the worker holding the task.
fields.label: Complete Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. Hand a task back with a MANDATORY reason and return it to the pool. The rejected assignment stays: it is the proof somebody was sent and could not do it.
fields.label: Reject Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. THE BRIDGE. Turns every open Compliance Alert into a dispatchable Farm Task carrying the evidence its completion has to produce. Idempotent — a second run finds the tasks the first raised and skips them.
fields.label: Generate Tasks from Compliance Alerts

fields.description: WRITE. The single-alert twin of generate_tasks_from_compliance_alerts — turns exactly one named alert into its dispatchable task, using the identical recipe lookup. Idempotent.
fields.label: Materialize Task for Alert

fields.description: READ. Every shape of recurring job this operation has defined — its skill, duration, evidence contract and checklist size. The map of what the operation knows how to ask for.
fields.label: List Farm Task Templates

fields.description: READ. One template in full: its evidence contract, its checklist item by item, which Compliance Rules raise work through it, and how many tasks it has produced.
fields.label: Get Farm Task Template

fields.description: WRITE. Define the shape of one recurring job as a record — type, skill, duration, dispatch mode, evidence contract, produced record, instructions and checklist. The next task raised from it has that shape, with no app release.
fields.label: Create Farm Task Template

fields.description: WRITE. Edit a template in place. It changes what FUTURE tasks look like and reaches nothing already raised — a task snapshots its template at creation.
fields.label: Update Farm Task Template

fields.description: WRITE. Raise one Farm Task pre-filled from a template. Location, assignee and urgency are the three overrides; everything else comes off the template.
fields.label: Create Task from Template

fields.description: READ. Every habitability walk, with the ones that found something and nobody closed named separately.
fields.label: List Housing Inspections

fields.description: READ. One walk in full, with its evidence and the unit's whole inspection history.
fields.label: Get Housing Inspection

fields.description: READ. Every smoke and CO detector test, with the failures and the buildings that have no detector at all.
fields.label: List Detector Tests

fields.description: READ. One test in full, with the building's testing history.
fields.label: Get Detector Test

fields.description: READ. Every agricultural water sample, with the contaminated ones nobody has resolved.
fields.label: List Water Tests

fields.description: READ. One sample in full: laboratory, results, report and the zone's testing history.
fields.label: Get Water Test

fields.description: WRITE. Record one habitability walk and move the unit's inspection date forward, which is what dismisses housing_inspection_overdue. The state is computed from the findings, never chosen.
fields.label: Record Housing Inspection

fields.description: WRITE. Correct or close one walk. Closing a finding requires a note saying what was actually done.
fields.label: Update Housing Inspection

fields.description: WRITE. Record a smoke and CO detector test and move the unit's detector dates forward. A Fail still writes the date; Not Present does not, because there is nothing to have tested.
fields.label: Record Detector Test

fields.description: WRITE. Correct a detector test or close its fault.
fields.label: Update Detector Test

fields.description: WRITE. Record one agricultural water sample and move BOTH the zone's and the parent block's test date forward. An unreadable result is not a clean result.
fields.label: Record Water Test

fields.description: WRITE. File the laboratory's answer against a sample taken days earlier, or close a contamination finding.
fields.label: Update Water Test
Mobile Accounts and Entity Scoping — Read

fields.description: Who has a phone, which of the six roles they hold, which entities their User Permissions actually allow, and what is wrong with each account. Reads the LIVE permission rows, so a scoping somebody changed in the Desk shows as drift. Turning this off hides the one report that would tell you an account is unscoped.
fields.label: List Mobile Users

fields.description: Who is calling, what they may do, and which entity the app should open on. The mobile app's first call after enrolment. The identity comes from the request's own credential, never from an argument on a request that already authenticated as somebody else.
fields.label: Current User Context

fields.description: Reach this site from outside over HTTPS and report the TLS certificate, the status and a verdict. Probes unauthenticated by default — a 401 is the best result. It will only reach the configured public_url or a host under .ts.net, because it makes an outbound request from inside your network.
fields.label: Validate Public Endpoint

fields.description: What this machine thinks it is serving: Funnel ports, URLs, the node's tailnet DNS name. Read-only, and nothing in this app can turn Funnel on or off — changing what is reachable from the whole internet is an operator decision.
fields.label: Tailscale Funnel Config

fields.description: What the authenticated caller is holding right now, with the tool each assignment is waiting for. The worker is resolved from the request through their Employee record, so the phone never has to know its own Employee id.
fields.label: My Tasks

fields.description: The pool the authenticated caller could take from, scoped to their entities. Honest about skills: nothing on a Frappe site records what skills a worker has, so an unfiltered pool comes back saying it is unfiltered rather than guessing from a job title.
fields.label: Pool For Me

fields.description: One task shaped for a screen: the job, and its evidence contract as a checklist with a satisfied flag and a capture hint per requirement. Same facts as get_farm_task, different reader.
fields.label: Task With Evidence Contract

fields.description: The compliance calendar narrowed to the entities the caller may see — one call per entity, merged, Critical first. An account with no Company User Permission is refused rather than shown the whole site.
fields.label: My Compliance Calendar

fields.description: READ. (Normalized operating cash flow − maintenance capex) ÷ productive acres, for one company over one period, WITH EVERY INGREDIENT ITEMIZED. The components are not extras: a normalized figure nobody can inspect is indistinguishable from an arranged one, and every buyer and lender who reads this number tests it one add-back at a time. Raw OCF is computed from GL Entry by the direct method so it traces back to rows; maintenance capex is actual spend and never a percentage of revenue; the denominator is what was PRODUCTIVE, time-weighted, not what is owned.
fields.label: Get Sustainable CF Per Acre

fields.description: READ. The normalization register — every adjustment proposed, approved, refused or superseded, with its justification and who signed it. Only Approved rows move the KPI, and the tool says which those are; the others are kept because a rejection with a reason teaches the next proposal.
fields.label: List Normalization Adjustments

fields.description: READ. Any registered financial report over a window, TRAILING TWELVE MONTHS BY DEFAULT, with the period just finished beside it and up to five years of prior windows under both. Agricultural revenue is aggressively seasonal — Q3 is harvest and Q1 is pruning — so two single periods set against each other say the operation collapsed in January and recovered in September, every year, on every farm. A rolling twelve months holds the whole cycle exactly once however it is read. The registry ships with sustainable_cf_per_acre, ocf and revenue.
fields.label: Get Windowed Report

fields.description: READ. The precomputed KPI cache as a plain time series, for drawing a line or exporting one. It reports what is NOT there as well as what is: a gap is a window nobody has computed yet, or one invalidated by a retroactively approved adjustment and not yet rebuilt, and it is not a period in which the business earned nothing.
fields.label: List Financial KPI History

fields.description: READ. The KPI register: what this site computes, how, over what window, and what it alerts on. v0.39.0 made a KPI a RECORD rather than a Python function, so every field on one — the window, the step, the lookback, the four thresholds, the dashboard order and the switch — is editable with no code release. What is NOT editable is the engine: formula_type has exactly two values, both deterministic, and nothing on the record holds Python.
fields.label: List Financial KPI Definitions

fields.description: READ. One KPI definition in full, with how much history is cached under it and whether it would compute at all. `problems` is the field to read: a Built-in naming a computer this site has not got, or an expression that no longer parses, produces nothing at compute time and says so in a warning rather than reporting a zero.
fields.label: Get Financial KPI Definition

fields.description: READ. One defined KPI over its own window, with the period just finished, the prior-window history and the threshold verdict beside it. It goes through the same window standard get_windowed_report does, so a KPI somebody typed into a form this morning behaves identically at the fiscal year boundary and on a partial ledger. A null value is an ANSWER — a division nobody could perform — and never a zero. It warms the Financial KPI History cache and writes nothing else.
fields.label: Compute KPI

fields.description: READ. The whole financial dashboard in one call: every enabled KPI for one company, in order, each with its value, its history and its threshold verdict. One broken definition does not empty the dashboard — it becomes a null value with a warning on that row. Read `breached` first and `unwatched_note` second: a KPI with no thresholds can never appear in `breached` however bad it gets.
fields.label: Compute All KPIs

fields.description: MUTATING. Proposes one add-back to or subtraction from operating cash flow. CREATES A DRAFT, ALWAYS — a draft does not count towards Sustainable CF/Acre and nothing in this tool can make it count. That split is deliberate: finding a non-recurring item in a ledger nobody reads line by line is worth a great deal, and deciding that it will not recur is a judgement somebody has to defend across a table.
fields.label: Create Normalization Adjustment

fields.description: MUTATING. THE HUMAN HALF. Sets an adjustment to Approved with the approver's signature attached and an approval timestamp written rather than taken as input. There is no unsigned path through it — the whole argument for the record is that a normalization is a judgement with somebody's name against it. Refused where another approved adjustment already covers the same company, period and category.
fields.label: Approve Normalization Adjustment

fields.description: MUTATING. Refuses a proposed normalization on the record, with the reason attached. The rejection is kept rather than deleted, for the same reason a rejected insurance claim is kept. An already-approved adjustment cannot be rejected — it has been counted, and rewriting a decision is not the same as recording one.
fields.label: Reject Normalization Adjustment

fields.description: MUTATING. Classifies Assets with no capex_type in bulk, dry-run by default. The heuristic is one sentence — everything bought before the operation started tracking is generally maintenance, because it is the existing productive plant carrying on — and it never overwrites a classification somebody made, so a second run finds nothing to do. A starting position rather than an answer, and it says so.
fields.label: Backfill Asset Capex Type

fields.description: MUTATING, and the only thing it can change is a CACHE. Rebuilds the precomputed history for one KPI; every row it writes is what the live computation would have produced, and every row it deletes comes back on the next read or the next overnight sweep. The answer to a retroactively approved normalization adjustment when the pack goes out this afternoon rather than tomorrow. Idempotent unless force=true, which clears the series and rebuilds it under the current code.
fields.label: Recompute KPI History

fields.description: MUTATING. Define one financial KPI as a record — what it is called, how it is computed, over what window, and what values are worth an alert. Two formula types and no third: Built-in delegates to a computer that ships with this app, and Expression evaluates arithmetic in a sandbox that parses to an AST and refuses every node that is not arithmetic. NOTHING ON THE RECORD HOLDS PYTHON, which is the deliberate difference from create_compliance_rule.
fields.label: Create Financial KPI Definition

fields.description: MUTATING. Edit one KPI definition in place — thresholds, window, order, description, the switch. It edits rather than superseding, unlike update_compliance_rule, because a rule is a definition behind an EVENT and a KPI is a definition behind a LINE. Changing the arithmetic is reported as a decision with the cached row count in front of the caller; kpi_id cannot be changed at all, because it is the cache key on every history row.
fields.label: Update Financial KPI Definition

fields.description: MUTATING, and the only thing it can change is a CACHE. Fills the cached history for one defined KPI or every enabled one; every row it writes is what the live computation would have produced, and every row it deletes comes back on the next read or the next overnight run. The answer to a changed formula (force=true rebuilds the series) and to a KPI created this morning, which has no history until the three-o'clock job reaches it.
fields.label: Refresh KPI Cache

fields.description: Whether the overnight Financial KPI History sweep runs. ON by default, because it is what makes a windowed report answer in a second rather than a minute — a five-year Monthly history is sixty full computations over twelve months of GL each, and the point of doing them at two in the morning is that nobody is waiting. Turn it off on a very large book or a shared bench: reports still answer, they answer from a cold cache, and they say in their warnings how much history they had to leave out. It does not affect recompute_kpi_history, which is somebody asking on purpose.
fields.label: Enable KPI History Overnight Sweep

fields.description: READ. One budget in full — every line item, every KPI target, and the breach state read from whatever was computed at its last refresh. `last_refreshed` is the field to check first: empty means every actual and variance figure is a placeholder rather than a figure.
fields.label: Get Budget

fields.description: READ. The budget register: every budget matching the filters, newest first, with its line item and KPI target counts.
fields.label: List Budgets

fields.description: READ. The full variance breakdown for one budget — every line item and every KPI target, and which of them breach their own threshold, worst first. Reads whatever refresh_budget last computed and never touches the ledger.
fields.label: Get Budget Variance Report

fields.description: MUTATING. Defines one budget: which general ledger accounts and which Financial KPI Definitions it tracks, and what it planned for each, for one company and one fiscal year. Every actual and variance column starts at zero — refresh_budget is what fills them in.
fields.label: Create Budget

fields.description: MUTATING. Edits one budget in place. line_items and kpi_targets, if passed, REPLACE the whole table — including every figure already computed on it — which refresh_budget then rebuilds.
fields.label: Update Budget

fields.description: MUTATING. Recomputes one budget's actual and variance columns from the general ledger (year-to-date GL movement within the fiscal year) and the KPI framework's own cache, and saves them onto the budget. Does not itself write a Compliance Alert — the budget_variance_breach rule reads these same stored fields the way financial_kpi_threshold_breach reads the KPI cache, and the hourly sweep is what reaches the calendar. The overnight sweep calls this for every Active budget automatically.
fields.label: Refresh Budget

fields.description: MUTATING. Sets status=Closed. Nothing is deleted — a closed budget keeps every figure it last computed and simply stops being refreshed overnight or scanned for variance alerts.
fields.label: Close Budget

fields.description: READ. One ML Model record in full — every field, its parsed class_names and metrics.
fields.label: Get Model

fields.description: READ. The model register: every ML Model matching the filters, newest first.
fields.label: List Models

fields.description: READ. THE TOOL AN iOS APP QUERIES to find out which model to pull for one company and one piecework activity. Returns the record and its manifest when a model is Active, or a clear 'nothing deployed yet' result — not an error — when none is.
fields.label: Get Active Model

fields.description: READ. One base64 slice of an ML Model's attached binary — the same shape stage_file_chunk takes, read backwards. Refuses by name when attach_model_file has not run yet.
fields.label: Get Model File Chunk

fields.description: READ. Which ML Model records are not in the current manifest schema, and what is outdated about each. Reads no files — the cheap metadata pass over the whole register. `blockers` names the records migrate_model_format cannot fix on its own.
fields.label: List Models Needing Migration

fields.description: READ. Holds one ML Model record's stored manifest to the current schema and reports every way it falls short — the manifest itself, the record against its manifest, and whether the attached file resolves and is the shape the manifest claims. Corrects nothing.
fields.label: Validate Model Bundle

fields.description: MUTATING. Registers a trained model from Volume Vision: which model it is, what it predicts, and which piecework activity it is for. Starts as Draft — activate_model is what makes it the model an iOS app pulls.
fields.label: Register Model

fields.description: MUTATING. Edits metadata on an existing ML Model record. status, company and piecework_activity cannot be changed here — activate_model/deprecate_model own status.
fields.label: Update Model

fields.description: MUTATING. Sets status=Active and deployed_at=now. Whichever other model was Active for the same (company, piecework_activity) auto-transitions to Deprecated — never more than one model is Active for one activity at one company.
fields.label: Activate Model

fields.description: MUTATING. Sets status=Deprecated. Nothing is deleted — a deprecated model keeps every field it had and simply stops being returned by get_active_model.
fields.label: Deprecate Model

fields.description: MUTATING. Gives an ML Model record the binary an iOS app pulls — the upload-once step that lets get_model_file_chunk serve it from ERPNext instead of an app reaching Volume Vision directly.
fields.label: Attach Model File

fields.description: MUTATING. Fetches a trained model straight from Volume Vision and attaches it — the bundle endpoint (/training/models/<uuid>/bundle) first, the original raw /download as a reported fallback. Makes an OUTBOUND request from this site's network to the host in the record's source_server; http/https only, no credentials in the URL, no redirects followed.
fields.label: Pull Model From Volume Vision

fields.description: MUTATING. Restates one ML Model record's manifest in the current schema. Metadata only — nothing is uploaded, downloaded or re-attached, and the binary is never read. A record that never had a bundle gets a manifest built from its own fields, saying so rather than claiming the labels came out of training.
fields.label: Migrate Model Format

fields.description: READ. Every Bucket Log Entry matching the filters, newest first.
fields.label: List Bucket Entries

fields.description: READ. The mock recall backwards: one lot back to the blocks, the crews, the pickers and the sprays that reached them.
fields.label: Trace Backward

fields.description: READ. The mock recall forwards: which lots carry product from a block, spray or water source, and which customers hold them.
fields.label: Trace Forward

fields.description: READ. One Bucket Log Session, with totals computed live from its own current entries.
fields.label: Get Bucket Session

fields.description: READ. The session register: every Bucket Log Session matching the filters, newest first.
fields.label: List Bucket Sessions

fields.description: READ. The payroll-ready summary for one employee over a date range: accepted buckets, sessions worked, acceptance rate.
fields.label: Get Piecework Summary

fields.description: READ. Compares accepted Bucket Log Entries against what Farm Payroll Slips actually paid for the same company and period, and flags discrepancies.
fields.label: Reconcile Bucket Payroll

fields.description: READ. Who holds this badge — the string a scanner produced, answered with the Employee (docname, name, designation, status, photograph). An unissued, retired or left-employee badge is refused with its own sentence rather than answered empty.
fields.label: Resolve Badge

fields.description: MUTATING. Receives a batch of bucket captures synced from a BucketLog device: creates Bucket Log Entry records, resolves employee from worker_badge, keeps the Bucket Log Session up to date. Deduplicates by entry_uuid.
fields.label: Sync Bucket Entries

fields.description: MUTATING. Maps a QR badge ID to an Employee, and backfills employee onto already-synced entries and sessions carrying that badge.
fields.label: Link Badge To Employee

fields.description: MUTATING. Associates Bucket Log Entries with a Farm Shift so they are picked up as piece units when that shift's payroll runs.
fields.label: Link Entries To Shift

fields.description: MUTATING. Issues (or reprints) one employee's scanning badge: mints a readable badge ID, records it in the Bucket Log Badge Map register, and returns the QR code for the card. regenerate=true retires the badge it replaces.
fields.label: Generate Employee Badge QR

fields.description: MUTATING. A printable sheet of badge cards for a crew at once — name, photograph, designation, badge ID and QR — issuing a badge to anybody who has none.
fields.label: Generate Employee Badge Sheet

fields.description: MUTATING. Draw one employee's ID card and attach it to their Employee record, so the badge sits in the Attachments sidebar of the form somebody already has open. Issues a badge if there is none and reuses the live one if there is. The card PDF needs wkhtmltopdf; without it the badge is still issued, the QR is still attached, and the result says what is missing.
fields.label: Generate Employee ID Card

fields.description: MUTATING. The employee's badge as an Apple Wallet .pkpass file and a Google Wallet save link — the same badge ID, QR payload and photograph as the printed card. Issues a badge to anybody who has none, the same way Generate Employee Badge QR does. A site with no Apple Pass Type ID certificate in site_config.json still gets a complete pass, marked unsigned; Apple Wallet refuses to open it until the certificate is installed. See docs/wallet-passes.md.
fields.label: Generate Employee Badge Pass

fields.description: MUTATING. Creates a Frappe User, assigns one of the six mobile roles, writes a Company User Permission per entity, and issues an API credential that is readable in the result exactly once. entity_access is mandatory and there is no override: in Frappe an account with no Company User Permission sees EVERY company on the site.
fields.label: Create Mobile User

fields.description: MUTATING. Creates one Employee record — the register every Farm Ops mobile method scopes work by. Writes seventeen identity, assignment and compliance-status fields and refuses everything else by name; payroll, tax and banking fields get their own refusal, because each has a form, an approval and a retention rule this app knows nothing about. The three statuses erpnext_mcp itself installs as mandatory — i9_status, w4_status, jurisdiction — start at Pending, Missing and the hiring entity's own state rather than blocking the hire, and every default is named in the result. Every Link and Select is checked against this site's own schema, and a second record for a name this company already has is refused with the existing docname.
fields.label: Create Employee

fields.description: MUTATING. Changes the same seventeen identity, assignment and compliance-status fields on an Employee that already exists, and reports field by field what actually changed with the previous value. Payroll, tax and banking fields are refused by name. Re-pointing an existing login needs replace_user=true — it moves that person's whole task history with it.
fields.label: Update Employee

fields.description: MUTATING. Sets Employee.user_id — the single field that turns a working mobile credential into a working task board. Reports whether the phone will now actually work, not merely whether the field was written: farm_ops_ready is true only when the account holds a Farm Ops role, its Mobile Access Grant is Active and the Employee is Active, and says which of the three is missing when it is not. One person, one login: refused when the User already belongs to another Employee.
fields.label: Link Employee To User

fields.description: MUTATING. One call for a new hire, in the only order that works: the Employee record, their I-9 / W-4 / photo ID filed as PRIVATE attachments ON THAT EMPLOYEE RECORD, a scoped login with a credential, THE LINK BETWEEN THE TWO, optionally the login QR, and optionally safety-training and camp-orientation tasks. The paperwork never goes to the governance archive — that register holds the documents describing the business, and an auditor, an advisor and a family member browse it. Idempotent: a second run reuses the Employee, the account and the link rather than duplicating any of them.
fields.label: Onboard Employee

fields.description: MUTATING. Disables a login, destroys its API credential and records WHY. The reason is required — 'left at the end of harvest' and 'dismissed for cause' are different answers to the same auditor question and the grant is the only place either survives.
fields.label: Revoke Mobile User

fields.description: MUTATING. Mints a fresh Frappe API key/secret for one user and RETURNS THE SECRET — the only time it appears in a result. Issuing a new one stops the previous one working. The expiry_days argument sets a REVIEW DATE, not an expiry: Frappe API secrets do not expire on their own and this app installs no job that revokes one.
fields.label: Generate API Token

fields.description: MUTATING. Destroys one user's API credential and leaves the account enabled. This is 'they lost their phone'; revoke_mobile_user is 'they no longer work here'.
fields.label: Revoke API Token

fields.description: MUTATING. A worker lost their phone: revoke the old credential, mint a new one, verify who they are by badge, and leave the Employee record untouched.
fields.label: Recover Mobile Access

fields.description: MUTATING. Produces a scannable PNG carrying the public URL, the user and a live credential. ANYBODY WHO PHOTOGRAPHS IT HAS THE ACCOUNT until the token is revoked. It expires for enrolment in 24 hours by default and rotates the secret by default, which invalidates any phone already enrolled. Refuses a non-HTTPS endpoint.
fields.label: Generate Mobile Login QR

fields.description: READ. Every Designation on this site with the number of ACTIVE Employees holding each, and the ones nobody holds. The register create_employee refuses an unknown designation against, which is what a hiring form should offer instead of a free-text box.
fields.label: List Job Titles

fields.description: READ. Every Department, optionally for one company, with its headcount. Reports BOTH spellings on every row — the docname Frappe built ('Harvest - OML') and the name somebody typed ('Harvest') — because they differ on any site with a company abbreviation.
fields.label: List Departments

fields.description: READ. Every Branch — the operating unit or camp somebody reports to, which on a farm is a different fact from which company employs them — with the number of Active Employees posted to each.
fields.label: List Branches

fields.description: READ. Every Employment Type with the number of Active Employees on each. Installing this app seeds Hourly and Seasonal Worker, because a stock Frappe HR ships neither and create_employee refuses a value naming no record.
fields.label: List Employment Categories

fields.description: READ. Every Employee Grade with the number of Active Employees on each. The LABEL and the headcount, not the pay: what a band actually pays is not read back here any more than it is written.
fields.label: List Pay Bands

fields.description: MUTATING. Adds one Designation — the register create_employee and update_employee refuse an unknown job title against. A Designation is also what a Position Wage Default is keyed on, so adding one creates the row a wage rate can hang off. Idempotent by name: a second call naming a title that exists is refused rather than creating a twin.
fields.label: Create Job Title

fields.description: MUTATING. Rewrites a Designation's description, or corrects its spelling. new_name goes through Frappe's own rename_doc, so every Employee already carrying the old title reads the new one without anybody editing them; it is refused where the target name already exists, because folding two registers into one is a decision about people rather than a typo.
fields.label: Update Job Title

fields.description: MUTATING. Adds one Department to a company's org chart. The one of the five org masters that belongs to a Company, and the one whose docname is not what you typed — Frappe HR appends the company abbreviation. Refuses a company the calling account cannot see.
fields.label: Create Department

fields.description: MUTATING. Moves a Department in the tree, retires it with disabled (which keeps the Employees already in it pointing at it), or corrects its spelling. Takes either spelling of the name.
fields.label: Update Department

fields.description: MUTATING. Adds one Branch — the operating unit or camp an Employee is posted to. Idempotent by name.
fields.label: Create Branch

fields.description: MUTATING. Corrects a Branch's spelling. A Branch carries nothing but its name on a stock Frappe HR site, so the rename is the whole tool — and it is a real need: a camp typed wrong at six in the morning is already on every person hired since. Refused where the target name exists.
fields.label: Update Branch

fields.description: MUTATING. Adds one Employment Type — H-2A, Salaried, Piece Rate, whatever this operation actually employs people on. Installing the app seeds Hourly and Seasonal Worker; this is how a site adds the rest. Idempotent by name, and the seeder is create-only in the same direction: neither overwrites what an operator has named.
fields.label: Create Employment Category

fields.description: MUTATING. Corrects an Employment Type's spelling and carries every Employee already on it. Refused where the target name exists: merging two categories changes what a whole group of people is classified as.
fields.label: Update Employment Category

fields.description: MUTATING. Adds one Employee Grade's LABEL. default_base_pay, default_salary_structure and default_leave_policy are REFUSED BY NAME — one value on a grade sets what an entire band of people is paid, which reaches further than any single Employee field this app writes, and it belongs in the Desk where the HR module's approvals run.
fields.label: Create Pay Band

fields.description: MUTATING. Corrects an Employee Grade's spelling and carries every Employee already on it. Its pay columns are refused by name here too.
fields.label: Update Pay Band

fields.description: MUTATING. claim_farm_task with the worker resolved from the authenticated request. Adds no rule and weakens none — the concurrent-claim limit and the refusal to self-pick Dispatched work still come from the same code.
fields.label: Claim Task (Mobile)

fields.description: MUTATING. start_farm_task with the worker resolved from the authenticated request. The clock-in for the task, not for the shift.
fields.label: Start Task (Mobile)

fields.description: MUTATING. complete_farm_task with the worker resolved from the authenticated request. Every refusal is unchanged, including the evidence contract check and the refusal of a completion filed by anybody but the worker holding the task.
fields.label: Complete Task (Mobile)

fields.description: READ. Completed task assignments grouped into the trips their handsets recorded — five cabins closed on one walk to the north block is ONE visit and five completions. The grouping is the app's `visit_id` rather than a guess from how close the timestamps are, because no threshold gets both an unhurried walk and two fast jobs at opposite ends of a property right. A completion with no visit_id is in no visit and is counted separately; everything filed before v0.20.1 is in that group.
fields.label: List Visits

fields.description: READ. Every Inspection Template on this site — the shapes of multi-section visit a worker can be sent on — with what each produces, which regimes it answers and which version is live. Superseded and deactivated templates are listed too, because the sessions worked from them are still readable.
fields.label: List Inspection Templates

fields.description: READ. One template in full: every section in working order with its evidence contract, its renderer hint, the compliance record it produces and the field prompts a client draws the form from. This is what a handset renders a sectioned visit from.
fields.label: Inspection Template Detail

fields.description: READ. Every templated visit — who went, where, from which template and which pinned version, and which compliance records the trip produced. The chain of custody an auditor follows backwards from a Housing Inspection to the afternoon that produced it.
fields.label: List Inspection Sessions

fields.description: READ. One visit in full: the pinned template version with all its sections, every section submission with what was ticked and measured, the shared evidence tray, and the compliance record each section produced.
fields.label: Inspection Session Detail

fields.description: MUTATING. Authors a new Inspection Template, live immediately — it reaches the handset on the next fetch and the rule engine can match it on the next sweep, with no app release. Templates are DATA: adding one is adding a record. Refuses a template with no sections, two sections sharing a name, a second live template with a name one already holds, and any evidence-contract key outside the vocabulary.
fields.label: Create Inspection Template

fields.description: MUTATING. Changes a template by SUPERSEDING it — a new row at version+1, the old one deactivated and pointing at it. The old row is never edited, which is why a session worked in April is still readable in November and why a session started against v1 while v2 is being authored is unaffected.
fields.label: Supersede Inspection Template

fields.description: MUTATING. Stops new sessions starting from a template, and records why. It destroys nothing — every session already worked from it stays readable and every compliance record they produced stays in the register and in the audit packet. There is deliberately no delete.
fields.label: Deactivate Inspection Template

fields.description: MUTATING. Opens one visit against one template at one place and pins the template version it will be read against. Writes NO compliance record and moves no register — a started session has dismissed nothing.
fields.label: Start Inspection Session

fields.description: MUTATING, AND THE ONE WITH TEETH. Files every section of a visit and writes the compliance records the sections promise — separately, at their own cadences, with the visit's shared evidence attached to each. Refuses a missing required section, a section the pinned template version does not have, and any section short of its evidence contract; nothing is written if any of those refuses, because half a visit is a set of records that look complete and are not.
fields.label: Submit Inspection Session

fields.description: MUTATING. An AI client that has read a regulation drafts an Inspection Template through this tool — its sections, their evidence contracts, the records they produce. The draft lands INACTIVE and marked `AI-proposed` with the source it was read from, so no handset fetches it until somebody approves it. No model is called here: the proposer IS the client, and this tool is the validator and the gate.
fields.label: Propose Template From Regulation

fields.description: MUTATING, AND IT IS THE GATE FOR TEMPLATES. An inactive template — one a model proposed, or one somebody withdrew — is turned on here and nowhere else, with the approver and the date written onto the record. Where a live template already holds the name at a lower version it is deactivated and pointed at this one: superseded, never edited, so the sessions already worked from it stay readable.
fields.label: Approve Inspection Template
Compliance rules (v0.22.0 — the rule definitions themselves)

fields.description: READ. One compliance rule in full: the condition it evaluates, its thresholds and scope filters, the regulation it cites, the kairotic gate saying what makes it ripe, and who approved it and when. Accepts a rule_id, which resolves to whichever version is live, or a docname, which is one exact version — including a superseded one, so the definition an older alert was raised under stays readable.
fields.label: Get Compliance Rule

fields.description: READ. Runs ONE rule against the data as it stands and reports every observation it WOULD make, with the alert docname each one would take, writing nothing. The tool to call between authoring a rule and approving it: a rule that observes four hundred rows is a rule whose condition is wrong, and finding that out here costs nothing.
fields.label: Test Compliance Rule (dry run)

fields.description: MUTATING. Authors a new compliance rule — a condition the nightly sweep evaluates against this site's records — with no code release. It arrives as a DRAFT and fires nothing until it is approved. Runtime stays deterministic: a rule is a declarative expression over record state, and there is no model in the trigger path. Refuses a duplicate rule_id, a target DocType this site has not got, a rule with no kairotic gate, a malformed scope filter, and any custom_python the sandbox would not run.
fields.label: Create Compliance Rule

fields.description: MUTATING, AND IT IS THE GATE. A rule cannot be enabled any other way — the DocType refuses `enabled` without an approver and a date — so there is no path by which a rule, least of all one a model proposed, starts firing without a person having put their name to it. An auditor asking who decided the site should watch for this reads the answer off the rule itself.
fields.label: Approve Compliance Rule

fields.description: MUTATING. Changes a rule by SUPERSEDING it — a new row at version+1, the old one disabled and pointing at it. The old row is never edited, which is why an alert from April is still explicable in November and why a sweep that started against v1 finishes against v1. The result carries a field-by-field before → after, so the audit log records what the rule said before and not merely what was asked for.
fields.label: Supersede Compliance Rule

fields.description: MUTATING. Stops a rule firing, and records why. It DISMISSES NOTHING — every alert it already raised stays on the calendar exactly as it was, because switching a rule off is not evidence that anybody did the work. There is deliberately no delete: the rule stays on the site, disabled, with the reason on the record.
fields.label: Deactivate Compliance Rule

fields.description: MUTATING. An AI client that has read a regulation drafts a Compliance Rule through this tool — target doctype, thresholds, scope, citation, kairotic gate. The draft lands DISABLED and marked `AI-proposed` with the source it was read from, and it fires nothing until a person approves it. A draft for a rule_id that is already live is written at version+1 and touches nothing; a draft carrying `custom_python` is flagged, and the approval refuses it until the approver acknowledges the code by name.
fields.label: Propose Compliance Rule

fields.description: READ. The regulation register: every source this site watches, with the regime it serves, how often it is checked, when it was last looked at and when it last moved. `status` is a report rather than a setting — Error is what the last check said, and Paused is the only state that keeps a feed out of the sweep.
fields.label: List Regulation Feeds

fields.description: READ. One source in full, including its append-only change log — every change, error and recovery it has seen, one timestamped entry each. A CHANGED entry names the rules derived from this source; it does not mean any of them was touched.
fields.label: Get Regulation Feed

fields.description: READ. Which regulations have moved since a date, and which compliance rules were written from them. The tool a quarterly compliance review opens with. The rules it names are a reading list rather than a changelog of the calendar: every one of them is still running on the definition a person approved.
fields.label: List Regulation Changes

fields.description: MUTATING. Registers a regulatory source — a URL, the regime it serves, what it covers, how often to look, and the compliance rules that were written from it. It writes a pointer and fetches nothing until a check runs. Refuses a URL that is not http(s), a feed name already on the site, a regime the vocabulary does not hold, and a rule link that resolves to nothing.
fields.label: Create Regulation Feed

fields.description: MUTATING. Edits a source, and pauses one — which is the kill switch, and keeps the whole change log. It CANNOT write the detector's own memory: the stored hash, the last-checked and last-changed timestamps and the change log are refused as arguments, because a hash somebody typed is a change that will never be reported.
fields.label: Update Regulation Feed

fields.description: MUTATING, AND IT MAKES AN OUTBOUND REQUEST. Fetches one source and compares a hash of its normalised text against the stored one. DETECTION ONLY: a change writes a hash, a timestamp and a log line naming the rules derived from that source, and modifies no rule at all. Ticking this lets an AI client ask a state agency's website a question on this site's behalf.
fields.label: Check Regulation Feed

fields.description: MUTATING, AND IT MAKES SEVERAL OUTBOUND REQUESTS. The sweep on demand: every source that is not paused and is older than its own check frequency, through the same code path the daily scheduler takes. One source's failure is one source's failure. It detects only — no compliance rule is read, modified, disabled or superseded by it.
fields.label: Check All Regulation Feeds

fields.description: READ. The asset register with type, location, scan status and retirement status.
fields.label: List Assets

fields.description: READ. One asset in full: current state, open tasks, history timeline from every doctype that references it, and child assets.
fields.label: Get Asset Detail

fields.description: READ. Chronological history of all events, tasks, inspections and compliance alerts for one asset.
fields.label: Get Asset History

fields.description: READ. Generate a QR code image for one asset's tag ID.
fields.label: Generate Asset QR

fields.description: READ. Bulk QR sheet for printing on Avery labels.
fields.label: Generate Asset QR Sheet

fields.description: WRITE. Record a scan event on an asset — updates last_scan_at, last_scan_by, and optionally the GPS position.
fields.label: Scan Asset

fields.description: WRITE. Register a new asset with its tag ID, type and location.
fields.label: Register Asset

fields.description: WRITE. Update an asset's fields. Cannot rename — the docname IS the tag ID.
fields.label: Update Registered Asset

fields.description: WRITE. Soft-retire an asset. Preserves all history; the asset drops out of active lists and compliance alerts.
fields.label: Retire Asset

fields.description: WRITE. Bulk registration for initial rollout — up to 500 assets in one call.
fields.label: Bulk Create Assets

fields.description: READ. List valid state-change actions for an asset given its current state and type.
fields.label: Get Available Actions

fields.description: WRITE. Log a state-change action on an asset — validates the transition, updates current_state, creates an immutable audit log entry.
fields.label: Log Asset State Change

fields.description: READ. Chronological state-change log for one asset.
fields.label: List Asset State History

fields.description: READ. Every capital asset (tractor, vehicle, implement, sprayer) as an insurance schedule line — serial/VIN, model, replacement value, location, date acquired, photo URLs — plus an itemised list of what is missing from it. Creates nothing.
fields.label: Export Insurance Schedule

fields.description: READ. How long the water ran: sums the open/close pairs in the Asset State Log for every valve at or below one asset, over a date window. Handles runs that cross the window's edges and reports still-running valves separately. Gallons only when a flow rate is given.
fields.label: Get Irrigation Runtime

fields.description: WRITE. Scan anything: resolves one scanned string against the badge register, Asset Register, Housing Unit and Field, in that order, and answers with the entity, its open work and what may be done next. It writes on the asset branch only — the same last_scan_at stamp Scan Asset leaves.
fields.label: Universal Scan

fields.description: READ. Valve runtime rolled up by zone, block, week, month, day or valve over a date range, priced per valve at its own Irrigation Zone's flow rate. Valves with no zone linked contribute minutes and no gallons, and are named rather than dropped. The report a water-rights filing is written from.
fields.label: Get Water Usage Report

fields.description: READ. Everything about one asset on one call: state, service status, engine hours, open tasks, compliance alerts, recent activity and any live restricted-entry interval on the ground it stands on. The same block scan_asset returns, for a caller who is not scanning — so it records no scan.
fields.label: Get Asset Status Report

fields.description: READ. What a tractor or vehicle has run: the meter now, hours this season, hours since the last service, and every checkout session paired with the hours on it. Computed from the Asset State Log series, not from a single overwritten column.
fields.label: Get Engine Hours Summary

fields.description: READ. Whether one asset — or every asset on the farm — is due for service, on hours, on the calendar, or on whichever comes first. A machine with an hours interval and no meter reading is reported as unmeasured rather than overdue.
fields.label: Check Maintenance Due

fields.description: READ. COMPLIANCE-CRITICAL. Is one block closed to entry after a spray, and until when. The longest live window wins. Defaults ON deliberately: a restricted-entry answer that an operator has to switch on is one a worker does not get at a gate.
fields.label: Get Active REI

fields.description: READ. COMPLIANCE-CRITICAL. Every block on the farm closed to entry right now — the board a foreman reads before sending anybody anywhere. Defaults ON for the same reason as Get Active REI.
fields.label: List Active REIs

fields.description: WRITE. Mark a service done — stamps last_service_date and last_service_hours, so the next interval counts from the right place.
fields.label: Record Service

fields.description: WRITE. Raise a Farm Task for every asset whose service is due. Skips assets that already have an open service task. dry_run defaults to TRUE — this raises work for other people.
fields.label: Trigger Maintenance Tasks

fields.description: WRITE. COMPLIANCE-CRITICAL. File a completed spray and open the restricted-entry window it creates — one Spray REI per block, from the longest REI in the tank. Refuses rather than writing a zero-hour window when no interval can be computed.
fields.label: Record Spray Application

fields.description: WRITE. Withdraw a restricted-entry window recorded against the wrong block. Cancelled rather than deleted, and the reason is required.
fields.label: Cancel Spray REI

fields.description: READ. The fill determination for one Bucket Log Entry or every entry in one session: mask area, container area, computed fill %, threshold applied, pass/fail.
fields.label: Get Fill Determination

fields.description: READ. The current fill threshold band for one container type at one company.
fields.label: Get Fill Thresholds

fields.description: READ. The audit log of every fill-threshold change, with each row's acknowledgment count.
fields.label: List Fill Threshold Changes

fields.description: READ. Which active Checkers have not yet acknowledged the current fill threshold for one container type.
fields.label: List Pending Threshold Acknowledgments

fields.description: MUTATING. Set the fill-percentage band for one container type at one company. Requires the Foreman role (or above) on top of this switch.
fields.label: Update Fill Threshold

fields.description: MUTATING. A checker acknowledges the current fill threshold for one container type. Idempotent.
fields.label: Acknowledge Threshold Update

fields.description: READ. One bin seal in full, with every contributor, the buckets attributed to each and the window their badge was scanning. `unattributed_buckets` is the checker's tally minus the badge scans and is reported rather than reconciled — a bucket tipped by somebody whose badge did not scan is in the bin and not in the rows, which is the fact a piece-rate dispute turns on.
fields.label: Get Bin Seal

fields.description: READ. The bin register by shift, field, block, tag, bucket session, checker or day. Contributors are deliberately not on it — one bin's crew is a child table, and forty bins would be forty reads of it.
fields.label: List Bin Seals

fields.description: READ. GIVEN A BIN TAG AT THE PACKING HOUSE, WHO PUT BUCKETS INTO IT — with the block, the shift and the checker. The accountability chain from the pack line back to the field, and the read the whole bin-sealing feature exists for. It answers with EVERY seal carrying the tag, because tags are reused between seasons and between growers and one confident answer about the wrong afternoon is worse than an ambiguous one. ON by default, because reading a trace cannot create one.
fields.label: Trace Bin

fields.description: MUTATING. Closes one bin and records whose buckets are in it — what the iOS tally screen posts when a checker seals. Idempotent on `client_event_id`, so a phone that did not hear the answer can retry without doubling a count at the pack line or a piece rate on somebody's cheque. OFF by default, like every other mutating tool: a bin count feeds a settlement, and turning it on is a decision an operator takes on purpose.
fields.label: Seal Bin

fields.description: READ. One lot with every Critical Tracking Event filed against it, its source lots and its status. Every break is NAMED rather than returned as an empty list: a lot with no events may simply not be indexed yet, and a lot with no block and no source lots is fruit whose origin was never written down. ON by default, because reading a trace cannot create one.
fields.label: Get Traceability Lot

fields.description: READ. The FSMA 204 lot register — by block, variety, day, status, shift or planting season, newest harvest first. Events and source lots are deliberately not on it: both are per-lot reads and forty lots would be eighty of them. ON by default.
fields.label: List Traceability Lots

fields.description: READ. Which lots carry this lot's fruit and WHO HAS THEM — the transformation graph walked downwards, then every Shipping event in that closure.
