Distinct from `trace_forward`, which walks the free-text bucket chain from a block or a spray; both are correct and they answer different questions from different evidence. It reports the fruit it CANNOT place, because the honest scope of a recall is wider than the destinations it can name. ON by default.
fields.label: Trace Lot Forward

fields.description: READ. Everything upstream of one lot — its source lots, their sources, the blocks at the roots, and then the spray register, bounded at each root lot's own harvest date. The spray hop is why it exists: a residue detection is a question about what a block had been given. Distinct from `trace_backward`, which walks the free-text bucket chain from a bin or a shipment. ON by default.
fields.label: Trace Lot Backward

fields.description: READ. The twenty-four-hour answer: everywhere a lot went, who received it, when. It WRITES NOTHING and sets nothing to Recalled — a drill is run on fruit nobody is worried about, and a read that changed a status would make the rehearsal indistinguishable from the event. Readiness is reported as a count, never as a verdict. ON by default.
fields.label: Recall Drill

fields.description: READ. One lot's events in the order they HAPPENED, with the referenced registers' rows resolved alongside — the document an audit asks for, in one call rather than one call per event. A pointer resolving to nothing is reported rather than dropped, and an uninstalled register is told apart from a deleted record. ON by default.
fields.label: Get Lot Timeline

fields.description: MUTATING. Assigns the one identifier FSMA 204 actually requires to one day's fruit off one block, as {block}-{variety}-{YYYYMMDD}-{sequence}. Idempotent on block, variety, day and company, because two codes for one afternoon's fruit split a recall in half and neither half names the other. OFF by default, like every other mutating tool: a lot code is printed on fruit and travels off the farm, and issuing one is a decision an operator takes on purpose.
fields.label: Create Traceability Lot

fields.description: MUTATING. Files one Critical Tracking Event — the FSMA 204 unit of record — against one lot. The event is a POINTER at the register holding the detail, never a copy of it. It never changes the lot: a Shipping event does not decrement a quantity or set a status, because those are separate measurements and a silent rewrite would make a lot disagree with its own history. OFF by default.
fields.label: Record Critical Tracking Event

fields.description: MUTATING. Sweeps one date window and attaches the Bin Seals, Scale Tickets and Spray Applications this site already holds to lot codes — creating the lots the seals imply. It is a TOOL rather than a `doc_events` hook because this app promises to install none, and running it here means an operator can see it, switch it off and re-run it over last season. Idempotent throughout, so a second sweep over the same window writes nothing. OFF by default.
fields.label: Index Lot Events

fields.description: READ. One Document Validation in full — the stored OCR text, the extraction it produced, the LLM assessment if one was supplied, and the status, confidence and human confirmation.
fields.label: Get Document Validation

fields.description: READ. The validation register, newest first, filterable by document type, source record and status. Carries neither the OCR text nor the extraction — get_document_validation has those.
fields.label: List Document Validations

fields.description: READ. Which stored validations are due to be re-checked, soonest first, with how many days each is overdue and how many have never been confirmed by a person. A document with no revalidation_due — a receipt, a signature — is never due and is excluded.
fields.label: List Revalidations Due

fields.description: MUTATING. Check what on-device extraction read off a scanned document against document-type-specific rules — a pesticide label's EPA registration number and its two intervals, a licence's expiry and holder name, a receipt's line sums — and store the answer as a Document Validation. This app makes no model call: the caller supplies its own assessment, and without one the status is Pending and an issue says so. Requires the Farm Manager, HR Manager, Foreman or System Manager role on top of this switch.
fields.label: Validate Document Extraction

fields.description: MUTATING. Re-run the checks against what a Document Validation already stores. Nothing is re-photographed and nothing is re-extracted — the stored OCR text and extraction are the input. Increments revalidation_count and stamps last_revalidated. Requires the same role as validate_document_extraction.
fields.label: Revalidate Document

fields.description:
Sprint 6 of the Gap Closure Plan (v0.71.0): the bank statement, and whether anybody can say what each line was.

Three questions that get confused and have different answers: is a transaction allocated in the ledger (ERPNext's own reconciliation), is there a receipt behind it, and does anybody know what kind of expense it was. get_bank_reconciliation_status answers all three side by side and never adds them together.

auto_match_receipts is a READ tool on purpose: it proposes and never commits, because a wrong link between a slip and a withdrawal is invisible afterwards — both documents exist and both amounts are right.
fields.label: CFL Banking — Read

fields.description: READ. Score every unmatched Expense Receipt against every unmatched bank withdrawal and return ranked proposals with the call that would commit each one. Writes nothing — a wrong receipt-to-bank link is invisible afterwards, so a person accepts each one.
fields.label: Auto Match Receipts

fields.description: READ. Three reconciliation questions for one account and period, answered separately and never added together: is each transaction allocated in the ledger, does each one have a receipt behind it, and does anybody know what kind of expense it was.
fields.label: Get Bank Reconciliation Status

fields.description: READ. Expense Receipts with no bank transaction against them — the evidence worklist — oldest first, with totals and a category breakdown.
fields.label: List Unmatched Receipts

fields.description: READ. Statement lines with nothing behind them, and which kind of nothing: no allocation in the ledger, no receipt on file, or both.
fields.label: List Unmatched Bank Transactions

fields.description: READ. The book of categorization rules in the order they are tried, with the ones that have never fired and the ones with no expense account named.
fields.label: List Bank Categorization Rules

fields.description: READ. What came in and what went out, with the bank statement reported apart from the documents and never summed with them, and a category breakdown that deduplicates a receipt against the withdrawal it is matched to.
fields.label: Get Cash Flow Summary

fields.description:
The write half of Sprint 6. Nothing here posts to the ledger — not one tool writes a GL Entry, a Journal Entry or an allocation. Matching a receipt records EVIDENCE; categorising records what a transaction WAS. Turning either into a posting is create_journal_entry, which has its own switch.

Categorisation is allowed to write in bulk where matching is not, because a rule is deterministic and its output names the rule that produced it — an operator who disagrees reads the rule, fixes it and runs again.
fields.label: CFL Banking — Write

fields.description: MUTATING. Link one Expense Receipt to the Bank Transaction it is the paper for, or rank the candidates and write nothing. Evidence, not a posting: nothing is booked and no allocation is made.
fields.label: Match Receipt To Bank Transaction

fields.description: MUTATING. Create one rule saying what a statement line is — description contains CHEVRON, category Fuel, account 5200. The expense account is never guessed.
fields.label: Create Bank Categorization Rule

fields.description: MUTATING. Run the enabled rules against uncategorised Bank Transactions and record the category, the account and which rule decided it. Posts nothing. Never overwrites a category set by hand unless asked.
fields.label: Apply Categorization Rules

fields.description: MUTATING. Put a starting book of farm categorization rules on the site — fuel, chemicals, parts, labor, irrigation, insurance, utilities, supplies, professional services, owner draw. Idempotent by (company, rule name): a second run creates nothing and leaves every edit alone. Disable a rule that does not fit rather than deleting it — a deleted rule is re-created by the next run.
fields.label: Seed Farm Categorization Rules

fields.description: MUTATING. Create a whole book of categorization rules from an array, vetted as a set before anything is written — which is what gets their priorities right relative to each other. A batch either produces the book you described or produces nothing.
fields.label: Create Bank Categorization Rules (Bulk)

fields.description:
The reconciliation chain: whether a year of bank data is complete. A transaction the feed never delivered leaves no row to inspect, so the only thing that finds it is opening balance + everything on file ≠ closing balance. Nothing in this section writes, posts or allocates.

ERPNext is the authority for this data as of v0.73.0; a bank pipe pushes anchors in through /api/method/erpnext_mcp.bank.push_statement_anchor and holds nothing itself.
fields.label: Bank Reconciliation Chain — Read

fields.description: READ. Every anchored statement period for one account, in period order, with the cumulative variance and any chain gap named. A chain gap is a MISSING STATEMENT, which no amount of per-transaction checking will find.
fields.label: Get Statement Anchor Chain

fields.description: READ. Every period that does not tie out, worst first by absolute variance, totalled per account. Periods with a recorded explanation are listed too — a known fact is not a problem, and hiding it makes somebody rediscover it every quarter.
fields.label: List Unreconciled Anchors

fields.description: READ. One period taken apart: what the statement said moved, what the transactions on file add up to, and the gap between the statement's own opening and closing balances — three sums that fail for different reasons and are never added together.
fields.label: Get Anchor Variance Breakdown

fields.description: READ. The lines a bank printed that no Bank Transaction accounts for — the one list that names a missing movement rather than just its size. Says so plainly when no statement lines are on file, because "nothing is missing" and "nothing to check against" are opposite answers.
fields.label: List Unmatched Statement Lines

fields.description: READ. The statement, the feed and the ledger for the same periods, side by side. Feed against ledger is the ordinary posting backlog; statement against feed is two independent records of one month that do not agree.
fields.label: Get Statement Recon Report

fields.description: READ. Bank accounts with their companion account and aggregator identity — mask, type, subtype, sync state — and the one-sided pairings called out by name.
fields.label: Get Account Pairing

fields.description: READ. One advisory agreement's terms, the assets under management they apply to, and what the fee should be — with the basis for the AUM always named, and a null fee rather than a zero one where none can be established.
fields.label: Get Advisory Agreement Summary

fields.description: READ. The register of advisory agreements, superseded ones included, plus the investment accounts with no active agreement on file — the accounts whose fees nobody can check.
fields.label: List Advisory Agreements

fields.description:
The write half of the consolidation. Nothing here posts to the ledger — not one tool writes a GL Entry, a Journal Entry or an allocation. An anchor says whether the books tie out; making them tie out is a Journal Entry somebody decided on, with its own switch.

rebuild_anchor_chain recomputes only DERIVED values by default and leaves the three numbers that came off a bank statement alone, because rewriting those from the transaction feed would make every period tie out perfectly and prove nothing.
fields.label: Bank Reconciliation Chain — Write

fields.description: MUTATING. Record why a period does not tie out, in one prose field. It does not mark the period reconciled and is not meant to — reconciled is arithmetic, and this is a human judgement beside it.
fields.label: Set Anchor Variance Reason

fields.description: MUTATING. Recompute the derived values on one account's chain in period order — closing, variance, reconciled, chain gaps and statement-line matches. Leaves the anchored opening, closing and statement transaction sum alone unless explicitly told otherwise.
fields.label: Rebuild Anchor Chain

fields.description: MUTATING. Link two Bank Accounts as companions and write BOTH sides. A pairing stored on one account and not the other reads as working from one end and absent from the other. Changes no transaction and no anchor.
fields.label: Pair Bank Accounts

fields.description: MUTATING. Register the terms an investment account is managed under. A fee type with no fee, and a second live agreement on one account, are both refused — each would compute a plausible wrong number rather than fail.
fields.label: Create Advisory Agreement

fields.description: MUTATING. Amend an agreement, which creates a new version and supersedes the old one rather than editing it — last quarter's fee was charged under last quarter's terms. Correcting a description in place is allowed; changing a fee, a date or a status in place is refused.
fields.label: Update Advisory Agreement
Interruption, Investigation and Discipline (v0.79.0)
fields.description: Field work is interrupted, investigations span days, and discipline is a chain. The two REGISTERS here are legally load-bearing: a progressive discipline chain is the defence in a wrongful-termination claim, and an accident investigation is what 29 CFR 1904 asks for. Their reads default ON for the same reason the REI reads do — a history an operator has to switch on is one nobody has when they need it.
WRITE. Stop the clock on a task a worker is coming back to. The minutes already worked are banked as a time segment; the gap is not charged to the job.
fields.label: Pause Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. Pick a paused task back up. Auto-pauses whatever else that worker had running — nobody is in two places at once.
fields.label: Resume Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. Record that two tasks are related, on both sides. Two people working one job on purpose, or two reports of the same thing.
fields.label: Link Farm Tasks

fields.description: WRITE. Fold a duplicate into the task actually being worked. Nothing merges itself: the evidence transfers, the duplicate goes to Merged pointing at the primary, and both sets of minutes stay countable.
fields.label: Merge Farm Task

fields.description: WRITE. Append a narrative entry to a Farm Task, Accident Report or Farm Incident Record. Entries are appended and never edited.
fields.label: Add Task Note

fields.description: WRITE. File a voice note and the transcription the handset produced on-device. The transcript is required, the recording is kept beside it.
fields.label: Attach Audio Note

fields.description: READ. A record's accumulated narrative, oldest first, with the whole thing assembled in order.
fields.label: List Task Notes

fields.description: WRITE. LEGALLY CRITICAL. File one step of progressive discipline, auto-linked to the prior step for that employee. Refuses an unexplained jump up the chain and a step after a termination.
fields.label: Create Farm Incident Record

fields.description: WRITE. Record that the employee acknowledged a step — or that they declined to sign, with a witness. There is no third outcome.
fields.label: Acknowledge Farm Incident Record

fields.description: READ. One discipline step in full, with its narrative and the step before it.
fields.label: Get Farm Incident Record

fields.description: READ. One employee's whole chain in order, with the current level and what the next step would be.
fields.label: List Incident History

fields.description: READ. The chain as a document for legal or HR review — the timeline, the narratives, and every documentation gap itemised with why it matters.
fields.label: Get Incident Report

fields.description: WRITE. Age a step out of the chain, or withdraw one on review. Nothing expires on a schedule in this app — the look-back window is a policy decision.
fields.label: Expire Farm Incident Record

fields.description: WRITE. OSHA-CRITICAL. Open an incident record at the scene with what is known in the first ten minutes. Everything else is filled in over the following days.
fields.label: Create Accident Report

fields.description: WRITE. Add findings, root cause and corrective actions to an open investigation. Called as many times as it takes; the narrative appends and is never edited.
fields.label: Update Accident Investigation

fields.description: WRITE. Close an investigation. Refuses without corrective actions, a follow-up date, a recordability determination, every witness statement taken and every sub-task resolved.
fields.label: Close Accident Investigation

fields.description: READ. One investigation in full: witnesses, narrative, sub-tasks, which days were worked, and what is still outstanding.
fields.label: Get Accident Report

fields.description: READ. The incident register, filterable by status, severity, recordability and date. Names every report whose recordability nobody has determined.
fields.label: List Accident Reports

fields.description: READ. The 29 CFR 1904 Form 300 log for one calendar year — one line per recordable case, numbered in the order they happened, each classified once at its most severe outcome. Reports of the year whose recordability nobody has determined are named separately rather than omitted silently: a log that hid them would present a partial year as a finished one.
fields.label: Get OSHA 300 Log

fields.description: READ. The Form 300A annual summary and the three rates computed from it — TRIR, DART and LTIR, each cases times 200,000 over hours worked. The hours come off the shift register or off the caller; where neither supplies them the rates are null rather than 0.0, because a zero rate reads as a perfect safety year.
fields.label: Get OSHA 300A Summary

fields.description: READ. One wizard's spec for a handset to render, resolved into the caller's language. Adding a flow is adding a record, not shipping an app.
fields.label: Get Wizard Definition

fields.description: READ. What flows this site can render, with their titles in the caller's language.
fields.label: List Wizard Definitions

fields.description: POLICY, not a tool switch. OFF (the default) means an incomplete document checklist is REPORTED and does not stop a shipment reaching Ready to Ship. ON means it holds the shipment until every required document is Approved or Sealed, unexpired, and carrying the reference its external filing returned — and releasing anyway needs a reason, which is written to the shipment. It ships off because a two-truck operation locked out of its own delivery by a certificate it will never need turns this module off entirely, and an operation that has turned it off gets no warnings either. One shipment can override this either way with its own Enforcement field.
fields.label: Enforce Trade Document Completeness

fields.description: READ. One shipment in full: the load, the route, every document on it, and whether it is ready to move.
fields.label: Get Shipment

fields.description: READ. The shipping register, filterable by status, customer, tier, destination country and ship date.
fields.label: List Shipments

fields.description: READ. Required versus done for one shipment, and exactly what is holding it — naming expired documents and those still waiting on somebody else's filing system.
fields.label: Get Shipment Readiness

fields.description: READ. One trade document in full, with its template's schema, what is still unfilled, and whether its seal still verifies.
fields.label: Get Trade Document

fields.description: READ. The document register, filterable by shipment, type and status. Names every document awaiting an external filing and every expired one.
fields.label: List Trade Documents

fields.description: READ. What kinds of trade document this site can issue, with their tiers, their schemas and whose system files them.
fields.label: List Trade Document Templates

fields.description: READ. What paperwork a destination asks for, before any shipment exists. A country's rules add to the tier's rather than replacing them.
fields.label: Get Destination Requirements

fields.description: WRITE. Open a shipment and build its document checklist from the destination's own rules. The checklist is a snapshot and is never silently rebuilt.
fields.label: Create Shipment

fields.description: WRITE. Walk a shipment forward. The one gate in this module is on Ready to Ship, it is advisory unless trade_document_enforcement is on, and an override writes its reason to the shipment.
fields.label: Update Shipment Status

fields.description: WRITE. Start one document for a shipment, populated from the record it is about where the template says where to look.
fields.label: Create Trade Document

fields.description: WRITE. Fill in a document's fields, its dates and the reference its external filing returned. Merges rather than replaces.
fields.label: Update Trade Document

fields.description: WRITE. Approve a document, with a Signing Evidence attestation over its fingerprint where the template asks for a signature. Requires a trade role.
fields.label: Approve Trade Document

fields.description: WRITE. Fingerprint an approved document and close it to editing. A hash over a row anybody can still edit proves nothing.
fields.label: Seal Trade Document

fields.description: WRITE. Bundle a shipment's documents into one tamper-evident record. Refuses unsealed documents unless told otherwise, and names them rather than dropping them.
fields.label: Generate Shipment Packet

fields.description: WRITE. Add or amend a kind of trade document. A new document type is a row, not a release.
fields.label: Create Trade Document Template

fields.description: WRITE. Configure what a destination asks for. A new export market is rows, not a release. Additive by default; replaced rules are disabled, never deleted.
fields.label: Set Destination Requirements

fields.description: IPO readiness Phase 1: spending authority, period close, and the checks a journal entry is put through before it is written. EVERY ONE OF THESE CONTROLS IS BYPASSABLE AND EVERY ONE SHIPS ADVISORY — it evaluates, files what it finds to the compliance calendar, and lets the work through. Turning one up to Enforced is done on its own Compliance Rule, not here; these switches decide only whether the TOOLS are reachable. The reads default ON, because an operator who cannot see which controls are set to what cannot make the decision the advisory season exists to inform.
fields.label: Financial Controls (v0.80.0)

fields.description: THE REGISTER OF WHAT THIS SYSTEM WILL AND WILL NOT STOP YOU DOING. Every transaction-time control this app implements, with the mode each one is set to on this site: Off, Advisory or Enforced. Read-only.
fields.label: List Control Points

fields.description: What the financial controls would say about a journal entry — a duplicate, an unusual amount, a closed period, a self-approval, a spend above somebody's authority. Read-only: NOTHING IS WRITTEN, no alert is filed, and nothing is refused however the controls are set.
fields.label: Check Journal Entry Controls

fields.description: One approval threshold with its chain, sorted the way the chain is EVALUATED rather than the way the grid was typed. Pass `amount` and it also answers the question you actually have: who has to release a transaction of that size. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Approval Threshold

fields.description: The spending-authority register: every threshold with its floor and its chain. A site with no threshold for a document type has expressed NO OPINION about authority for it, which is reported as such rather than read as unlimited. Read-only.
fields.label: List Approval Thresholds

fields.description: One accounting period: every step with who ticked it and when, what is still outstanding, and whether the period is locked against posting. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Closing Checklist

fields.description: The period register, most recent first, with each period's outstanding count and lock state. This is the read that answers 'which months are actually closed'. Read-only.
fields.label: List Closing Checklists

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Define who may release a transaction of a given size: an auto-approve floor beneath which nothing needs releasing, and a chain of rungs above it saying which ROLE may release up to which amount.
fields.label: Create Approval Threshold

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Change a threshold's floor, currency, document type, enabled state or chain.
fields.label: Update Approval Threshold

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Open an accounting period with the steps that have to be finished before it closes. Give no steps and the eight a month-end close almost always has are seeded, in English and Spanish, every one of them required and every one editable.
fields.label: Create Closing Checklist

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Edit a period's dates, type, status, notes or steps. DOES NOT LOCK OR UNLOCK — close_accounting_period and reopen_accounting_period do that, so a period can never be locked as a side effect of fixing a typo.
fields.label: Update Closing Checklist

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Tick one close step, recording who and when. Pass `evidence` — a reconciliation docname, a report reference, a journal entry — because a checklist of bare ticks is a claim and a checklist of ticks that each point at something is evidence.
fields.label: Complete Checklist Item

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Lock a period against posting.
fields.label: Close Accounting Period

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Unlock a closed period. A reason is REQUIRED and goes on the record.
fields.label: Reopen Accounting Period

fields.description: IPO readiness Phases 2 and 3. REVENUE: the ASC 606 unit of account — what was promised, how the price is allocated between the promises, when each is earned — plus the contract-to-cash trace an auditor's question actually reduces to. COST: a growing crop carried at a value with its remeasurements behind it, what things are supposed to cost, and the variance between that and what they did. The reads default ON; every write is off until an operator turns it on, including recognize_revenue_milestone, which produces a DRAFT journal entry and never posts.
fields.label: Revenue Recognition and Cost Accounting (v0.80.0)

fields.description: One contract in full: every performance obligation with whether control has transferred, the recognition schedule with what has been drawn and what is left, and any settlement statements linked to it. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Revenue Contract

fields.description: The contract register with each one's recognition progress, and the totals across them: contracted, recognised, and still to recognise. Read-only.
fields.label: List Revenue Contracts

fields.description: THE WHOLE CHAIN FOR ONE CONTRACT: contract → settlement → invoice → payment → GL entries, each hop with its date, its amount and its docname. Read-only.
fields.label: Trace Contract To Cash

fields.description: One growing crop with its FULL valuation history, oldest first, plus the movement between the first and the latest. The sequence is the evidence: a current value with no trail behind it is an assertion nobody can test. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Biological Asset

fields.description: The growing-crop register with each asset's carrying value and the total across them. ASSETS THAT HAVE NEVER BEEN VALUED ARE EXCLUDED FROM THE TOTAL and counted separately, rather than added in as zero — a carrying value that silently included un-valued crops would understate the balance sheet and look like a measurement. Read-only.
fields.label: List Biological Assets

fields.description: One standard by docname — or, given `subject` and `on_date`, THE STANDARD THAT COVERED THAT DAY. It refuses rather than picking the nearest when nothing covered the date, because a variance against the wrong season's standard is a confident wrong number. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Standard Cost

fields.description: The standards register. Pass `on_date` to collapse it to the one standard per subject and basis that covered that day, which is what a costing run wants. Names the standards whose actual side cannot be read from the ledger. Read-only.
fields.label: List Standard Costs

fields.description: Actual against standard, per subject, with the gaps past each standard's own tolerance flagged. THE COMPARISON IS THE CONTROL — a standard nobody compares against is a number in a table. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Cost Variance Report

fields.description: Cost from field through packhouse, per unit, with overhead absorbed or excluded. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Absorption Cost Report

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Record what was promised to a customer, what it is worth, and when each part of it is earned — the ASC 606 unit of account.
fields.label: Create Revenue Contract

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Revise a contract's transaction price, status, accounts, obligations or schedule — and mark an obligation SATISFIED, which is what makes its milestone tranche recognisable.
fields.label: Update Revenue Contract

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Attach a settlement statement to the revenue contract it settles — the join that makes contract-to-cash traceable in one hop. A settlement is where a consignment pool stops being an estimate and becomes a number, which is the moment ASC 606's variable consideration resolves.
fields.label: Link Settlement To Contract

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Recognise one scheduled tranche, producing a DRAFT journal entry that debits the receivable account and credits the revenue account.
fields.label: Recognize Revenue Milestone

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Register a growing crop carried at a value — an orchard block, an annual planting, a nursery lot.
fields.label: Create Biological Asset

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Change a crop's type, status, ground or cost center.
fields.label: Update Biological Asset

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Remeasure a growing crop, APPENDING to its valuation history. IAS 41 remeasures at each reporting date and the sequence is what an auditor tests, so this never overwrites — `current_value` simply follows the newest row.
fields.label: Record Biological Asset Valuation

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Define what a thing should cost — per bin, per acre, per hour — for a date range.
fields.label: Create Standard Cost

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Change a standard's rate, date range, classification or tolerance. CLOSING ONE IS HOW A NEW SEASON'S IS MADE: set `effective_to` on the current row, then create the next — the overlap check then guarantees there is never a day with two answers to 'what should this have cost'.
fields.label: Update Standard Cost

fields.description: IPO readiness Phases 4 to 6, the governance domain. RELATED PARTIES: which transactions were with them, whether each was priced at arm's length on paper, and what the year-end schedule says. ITGC: who holds which permissions and when somebody last looked, what changed and who approved it, and whether a backup has ever actually been restored from. REPORTING: the shape of a periodic report, the numbers a management discussion is written from, and the checklist that says a filing is finished. The reads default ON and none of them ever refuses — that is what lets an operation see exactly what enforcement would do before switching it on. Every write is off until an operator turns it on. All five control points ship ADVISORY.
fields.label: Governance, ITGC and Disclosure (v0.81.0)

fields.description: Every transaction in a window that was with somebody on the related-party register, each stamped with whether an arm's-length case covers it. A name match is always labelled as one and anything that resolved to nothing is reported rather than dropped — the commonest way a related-party schedule is wrong is a relationship nobody wrote down.
fields.label: Get Related Party Transactions

fields.description: The disclosure register: every relationship that has to be disclosed, what was transacted with it, and the gaps behind each — no governing document, no Supplier linked, undocumented transactions, every memo still a draft.
fields.label: List Related Party Disclosures

fields.description: The related-party schedule for a period, with the pricing methods relied on. A WORKING PAPER: nothing is filed, stored or attached.
fields.label: Generate Related Party Disclosure

fields.description: One transfer pricing memo in full, plus the transactions in its period it actually covers.
fields.label: Get Transfer Pricing Doc

fields.description: The memos on file, split by status, naming the Complete ones reviewed by the person who wrote them — which is not a review.
fields.label: List Transfer Pricing Docs

fields.description: Who has what, computed now and STORED NOWHERE: every login, its roles, what those roles reach, last login. A permissions snapshot in a table is wrong the moment somebody adds a role.
fields.label: Generate Access Control Report

fields.description: One recorded system change in full.
fields.label: Get Change Management Log

fields.description: The change log, newest first, calling out changes with no approver and changes approved by their own author.
fields.label: List Change Management Logs

fields.description: The change control picture for a period — volume, approval rate, what is outstanding — and how much of the log this app wrote about its own calls versus how much somebody typed.
fields.label: Get Change Management Report

fields.description: One backup event, with whether its test restore met the recovery time objective.
fields.label: Get Backup Record

fields.description: Backups on file with the verification picture: how many have ever been restored from, which have never been tested.
fields.label: List Backup Records

fields.description: One report shape in full, labels in the caller's language, with the untranslated ones named.
fields.label: Get Reporting Template

fields.description: What report shapes this site has, without pulling every section of every one.
fields.label: List Reporting Templates

fields.description: The figures a Management Discussion and Analysis is written FROM. Not a draft: the evidence pack, honest about every source it could not read.
fields.label: Generate MD&A Data Feed

fields.description: Revenue, expense and result by cost centre with ASC 280's ten-per-cent test APPLIED AND SHOWN — never decided, because whether these are operating segments is a judgement no query can make.
fields.label: Generate Segment Report

fields.description: One checklist in full, with what enforcement would say about finalising it as it stands.
fields.label: Get Disclosure Checklist

fields.description: Checklists on file, including any marked Filed while required disclosures were outstanding.
fields.label: List Disclosure Checklists

fields.description: The pieces assembled: sections, their sources, the figures where this site could produce them, and every gap. Contains no prose and never will.
fields.label: Generate Quarterly Report Skeleton

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Run one dealing through the transfer pricing control and file what it finds. Advisory reports and lets the work through; Enforced reaches the same finding, writes the same alert, and refuses.
fields.label: Flag Related Party Transaction

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Record the arm's-length case for one related-party arrangement: the price, what it was tested against, and why the two agree. Arrives as a DRAFT, and a draft covers nothing.
fields.label: Create Transfer Pricing Doc

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Change a memo, including promoting it to Complete — which is refused while the justification, the market rate reference or the pricing method is empty.
fields.label: Update Transfer Pricing Doc

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Record one system change. An approver who is the person who made the change is refused outright; a one-person finance function records that honestly as Not Required with the compensating control in the notes.
fields.label: Create Change Management Log

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Record that a backup ran. It arrives unverified and stays that way until somebody actually restores from it.
fields.label: Create Backup Record

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Record a test restore — the event that turns a backup job into a control. Only a Pass verifies; 'Not Tested' is refused as a result.
fields.label: Record Backup Test

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Define the shape of a periodic report: its sections, in order, and which tool on this site fills each.
fields.label: Create Reporting Template

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Change a template. Sections are restated whole rather than merged, because the only stable row key is the section name and that is what a rename changes.
fields.label: Update Reporting Template

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Open the checklist for one filing: which disclosures it must make, what requires each, and who owes it.
fields.label: Create Disclosure Checklist

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Change a checklist. Moving it to Complete or Filed is a claim, and it is the moment the completeness control is consulted — before anything is written.
fields.label: Update Disclosure Checklist

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Settle one disclosure. Not Applicable is a completed state and REQUIRES a reason — the reason is the disclosure; Outstanding is not settled and neither is In Progress.
fields.label: Complete Disclosure Item

fields.description: The QR valve workflow: scan a tag, see the state and today's runtime, toggle it. No register of its own — a valve is an Asset Register row of type "Irrigation Valve", so these switches gate the workflow and the asset tag switches still gate the register underneath it.
fields.label: Irrigation Valve Workflow

fields.description: READ. Every valve, or every valve on one zone, with its state, rank, zone, parent and child count. A valve never toggled resolves as closed rather than unknown.
fields.label: List Irrigation Valves

fields.description: READ. One valve in full: state, zone and its flow rate, the chain of valves above it, the valves below and which are open, today's runtime for the valve and for everything it commands, and what one press of the toggle would do.
fields.label: Get Irrigation Valve

fields.description: READ. Hours one valve ran over a date window with its whole zone's total beside it. The same measurement Get Irrigation Runtime makes, scoped to a valve and its zone.
fields.label: Get Valve Runtime

fields.description: WRITE. Register one valve on a line: tag ID, rank (Main, Sub-Main, Lateral), the zone it draws through and the valve upstream of it. Refuses a Main filed underneath a Lateral, which the closing cascade would otherwise honour.
fields.label: Create Irrigation Valve

fields.description: WRITE. Open a closed valve, close an open one, reading the state so the caller does not have to. CLOSING CARRIES DOWN THE LINE — every valve below is closed too and each gets its own log row. Opening does not cascade. Refuses a winterized or retired valve.
fields.label: Toggle Irrigation Valve

fields.description: WRITE. Resolve a scanned valve QR and answer with the whole valve screen. It writes the scan stamp only — last_scan_at, last_scan_by and the GPS fix, the same stamp Scan Asset leaves. It does NOT toggle the valve.
fields.label: Scan Valve QR

fields.description: Activity-based costing. WHAT IT ANSWERS is the question a chart of accounts cannot: what did the Home Block cost per acre. Spend arrives labelled by supplier and by account, never by block, so ABC gathers cost into a POOL per ACTIVITY and then pushes each pool out by how much of that activity each block actually consumed. Every run is stored whole — driver quantity, share, pool, amount and acres on every line — because a per-acre cost is a quotient of two numbers that both moved during the year. THE ENGINE NEVER ESTIMATES A DRIVER: acres are derived from the Field register and a direct assignment comes off the pool, and every other driver is a measurement somebody supplies or the activity is reported unallocated with its full amount. The six reads default ON; the four writes are off until an operator turns them on.
fields.label: Activity-Based Costing (v0.84.0)

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Define one thing the operation does that costs money — spraying, pruning, irrigating, picking. `cost_driver` decides how every dollar in its pool reaches a block, and `phase` decides where on the cost waterfall that money enters.
fields.label: Create Cost Activity

fields.description: One activity with its ledger scope, its accounts and every pool ever built for it. Says plainly whether its driver is derivable or a measurement somebody has to supply. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Cost Activity

fields.description: The activity register with what each one's cost is divided by, counted by phase — and the activities whose drivers this app cannot derive, which are the ones that come back unallocated if nobody measures them. Read-only.
fields.label: List Cost Activities

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Change an activity's type, phase, driver, ledger scope or accounts. Stored runs are NOT restated — a line carries the phase and driver it was computed under.
fields.label: Update Cost Activity

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Gather one activity's cost for one fiscal year into a pool, totalled off the ledger and itemised by account, or recorded as Manual where the figure is supplied. The difference is a column rather than a footnote.
fields.label: Create Activity Cost Pool

fields.description: Every pool for a company and year with the ledger/manual split separated out, because a typed figure and a read one are different kinds of evidence. Read-only.
fields.label: List Activity Cost Pools

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Run the allocation engine and store the whole run, intermediates and all. It will not estimate a driver quantity: an activity whose measurements never arrived is reported unallocated with its full amount rather than spread evenly across blocks.
fields.label: Compute ABC Allocation

fields.description: One stored allocation run in full — every line with the driver quantity, share and acres it was computed from. Read-only.
fields.label: Get ABC Assignment

fields.description: Per-acre cost grouped by field, activity or phase — the primary management report. The denominator changes with the grouping and every row says which it used. Read-only.
fields.label: Get ABC Report

fields.description: Cost accumulating through Growing → Harvest → Post-Harvest → Packing → Sales. The shape is the answer, not the total. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Phase Waterfall
Multilingual Support (v0.85.0)
fields.description: The string register: what a worker reads, in the language they read it in. A missing translation SERVES ENGLISH AND SAYS SO — never a blank, never the raw key, never a refusal. Employee.preferred_language is the authority and Accept-Language is only the fallback, because this app's claim to have communicated a hazard 'in a manner the employee can understand' rests on a column somebody filled in about a person, not on a device setting.
READ. What this site says, in which languages, and which keys are missing a translation — which is the question this tool mostly exists to answer.
fields.label: List Translations

fields.description: READ. One key resolved into the caller's language, with what it says in every other language and whether this answer fell back to English.
fields.label: Get Translation

fields.description: WRITE. Write or correct one string in one language. The row becomes operator_edited and no later migrate overwrites it. Placeholders are checked against the English and a mismatch is refused before anything is written.
fields.label: Update Translation
Shadow Log RACI Feed (v0.85.0)
fields.description: A frozen copy of what happened, addressed up the chain of command. Not a notification: each copy carries the source record's values AT THAT MOMENT, so an acknowledgement cannot silently migrate onto a later correction — and three levels holding three copies is a redundant backup that survives the original being deleted.

Whether a bucket sync, a shift close, a raised compliance alert and a completed farm task write supervisory copies AT ALL. NOT a tool switch — the three tools below stay usable for rows already written. Ships ON, because the feed is the feature; an operation with no chain of command (a two-person orchard where everybody is the owner) turns it off and stops generating rows nobody reads. Turning it off NEVER fails the work being filed: propagation could not do that in any case, by construction.
fields.label: Shadow Log Feed Enabled

fields.description: READ. What went up the chain: one frozen copy per level per event, filtered by recipient, level or whether it has been acknowledged.
fields.label: List Shadow Log Entries

fields.description: READ. One copy in full: the frozen snapshot, whether its hash still matches it, and whether the source record still exists.
fields.label: Get Shadow Log Entry

fields.description: WRITE. Record that the recipient has seen one copy. ONE-WAY — an acknowledgement cannot be withdrawn — and safe to retry. Writes nothing to the source record.
fields.label: Acknowledge Shadow Log

fields.description: The breakeven calculator. A Breakeven Analysis is a PERSPECTIVE on the chart of accounts the farm already keeps — nothing here posts, nothing is a journal entry, and no number it produces changes what the financial statements say. What it adds is the one thing a chart of accounts cannot hold: which accounts stop mattering when the crop gets bigger. The three reads default ON and none of them ever refuses. The two writes are off until an operator turns them on, and both are 'mutating' because they STORE — the cost lines, the results and the scenario band go onto the analysis, which is what makes this season's breakeven comparable with next season's.
fields.label: Breakeven Calculator (v0.87.0)

fields.description: One analysis in full: the inputs, every cost line with WHO CLASSIFIED IT, the stored scenario band, and the market overlay. It says when its numbers are not answers — a Draft has never been computed and a Stale one had an input changed after the last run. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Breakeven Analysis

fields.description: The register, with the headline number on every row — breakeven price, contribution margin, margin of safety. Names the ones that are NOT answers: never computed, stale, and the ones where no volume breaks even at all. Read-only.
fields.label: List Breakeven Analyses

fields.description: What-if over ONE variable across a range: price, yield, packout, fixed cost or variable cost. Reports how far the breakeven price moved across the whole band, which is the figure that says whether this is the term worth managing. Stores nothing. Read-only.
fields.label: Get Breakeven Sensitivity

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Register a crop, a volume and a price to model — the record behind 'what price do I need to break even?'. Nothing is posted and nothing is computed: creation and computation have separate switches on purpose.
fields.label: Create Breakeven Analysis

fields.description: MUTATING (default OFF). Read the company's expense accounts, sort them into fixed and variable, and answer the question — breakeven units, breakeven revenue, contribution margin per unit, and THE BREAKEVEN PRICE. Mutating because it STORES, not because it posts: the ledger is not touched. This is also where the packout slider lands.
fields.label: Compute Breakeven

fields.description: Where the market overlay's prices come from. USDA AMS Market News publishes shipping point prices — what a district was asking f.o.b. — and this app keeps every quotation it sees in the USDA Price Quote register. THE OVERLAY READS THE REGISTER, NOT THE INTERNET, which is what makes it work in a farm office whose link is down and on a site that has never configured a key at all. None of this is needed to compute a breakeven; it answers the second question, 'is the market currently paying that?'
fields.label: USDA Market News (v0.87.0)

fields.description: An API key for the USDA MARS API, obtained free from AMS. Held in a Password field, so it is encrypted at rest and never returned by any tool — the same contract the MCP bearer token above carries. Without one, nothing is ever fetched and the overlay reads whatever quotations are already on the site, including prices somebody typed in from a broker's bid.
fields.label: USDA MARS API Key

fields.description: Override the MARS API base URL. Leave empty for the shipped default (https://marsapi.ams.usda.gov/services/v1.2). Set it only to pin a different API version or to point at a cache inside your own network.
fields.label: USDA API Base URL

fields.description: Whether the overnight sweep fetches the reports named below. SHIPS OFF, unlike the weather sweep, and the difference is that weather works out of the box against a keyless public API while this does not: a nightly job that cannot authenticate would write a failure to the error log every night on every site that never wanted a market overlay. Turn it on in the same visit as entering the key.
fields.label: Enable USDA Price Sweep

fields.description: Which AMS reports the sweep pulls, by slug, comma- or newline-separated. NO DEFAULTS ARE SHIPPED, deliberately: AMS identifies its reports by slugs an operator looks up for the districts and commodities they actually ship into, and a list invented here would be right for one region and a nightly 404 for everybody else. An unconfigured sweep does nothing and says so.
fields.label: USDA Report Slugs

fields.description: READ. The crop register with varieties counted, plus the crops carrying no pre-harvest interval, no harvest window and no varieties.
fields.label: List Crops

fields.description: READ. One crop in full: varieties, rootstocks, pollination groups, water demand by growth stage, and the markets that buy it. Warns when every recorded variety sits in one pollination incompatibility group.
fields.label: Get Crop

fields.description: READ. One variety's resolved care recipe: its water schedule with each Kc and weekly depth resolved against the crop default PER FIELD and labelled with which record it came from, plus its cultural practice protocol — GA timings, PGR program, thinning and pruning — grouped by practice. Reports the catalogue rootstock and says outright that the binding one is on the block's planting.
fields.label: Get Variety Care Recipe

fields.description: READ. The market register with grade standards counted, plus the active markets with no grades — which is the list that says which breakeven assumptions have nothing behind them.
fields.label: List Markets

fields.description: READ. One market in full, its grade ladder sorted by what each grade pays, and the premium spread across that ladder.
fields.label: Get Market

fields.description: READ. Which units are valid for which work — harvest counts containers, spray measures volume, ground is measured in acres, a scale reports weight.
fields.label: List Agricultural UoM Contexts

fields.description: READ. How many of one unit are in another, for a given crop. Inverts and chains one hop, and always says whether the factor was crop-specific or the generic fallback.
fields.label: Get UoM Conversions

fields.description: WRITE. Register a crop with its varieties and its water demand by growth stage. Refuses a duplicate, half a harvest window, two varieties of one name, and years-to-maturity on an annual.
fields.label: Create Crop

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered crop. Cannot re-key it — the docname is the crop name every other record spells. Child tables are replaced wholesale, never merged.
fields.label: Update Crop

fields.description: WRITE. Register a market with its grade standards. Sizes in millimetres rather than row sizes, which are an inverse scale. Negative premiums are accepted; a defect tolerance outside 0-100 is not.
fields.label: Create Market

fields.description: WRITE. Change a registered market, including retiring it. Cannot re-key it — last season's settlements spell the docname. The grade ladder is replaced wholesale.
fields.label: Update Market
Spray Program — Tank Mixes, Nozzles and Applications

fields.description: READ. Every nozzle set on file — tip type, pattern, flow rate per nozzle, rated pressure and ASABE droplet class. Retired sets are hidden unless asked for.
fields.label: List Spray Nozzle Configs

fields.description: READ. COMPLIANCE-CRITICAL. Spray applications over a window — product and rate, block and acres, applicator and licence, and the weather at the time. This is the pesticide record a state inspector asks for. Names the passes with no wind speed recorded, which cannot be reconstructed afterwards.
fields.label: List Spray Applications

fields.description: READ. COMPLIANCE-CRITICAL. One spray in full — the tank as applied, every block and its acres, the weather, the label intervals, and which blocks are still restricted right now. The live restrictions are read through the Spray REI register rather than recomputed, so they stay correct after a window is cancelled.
fields.label: Get Spray Application

fields.description: READ. Chemical usage over a period, grouped by product and then by block: total quantity per product, which blocks received it, on what dates, by which applicator, and the label intervals it carried. The pesticide use report a state asks for. Quantities are summed per unit and never across units.
fields.label: Get Spray Application Report

fields.description: WRITE. Register one nozzle set as it is plumbed on a boom or air-blast tower. Flow rate is per nozzle off the manufacturer's chart, not the boom total.
fields.label: Create Spray Nozzle Config

fields.description: WRITE. Write a tank mix — several products in one tank, each at its OWN rate per acre, optionally split across two nozzle sets flipped mid-pass. Computes the longest REI and PHI in the tank and copies each label's numbers off its Item at mix time. Refuses a dual mix with nothing on one side.
fields.label: Create Spray Tank Mix

fields.description: WRITE. COMPLIANCE-CRITICAL. File a spray — what went out, over which blocks, when, by whom, in what weather — and open one Spray REI window per block. Unlike Record Spray Application it does NOT refuse a tank with no label interval: a foliar nutrient restricts nobody and is still a real pass, so it records the application and creates zero windows. Weather outside the label range is an advisory on the record, never a refusal.
fields.label: Create Spray Application
Crop Protection — Observation, Pressure and IPM

fields.description: READ. Every action threshold on file — how many of a threat, on a crop, at a growth stage, before somebody acts. Names the thresholds with no recommended methods, which generate an alarm rather than something a crew can act on.
fields.label: List Pest Action Thresholds

fields.description: READ. Scouting records over a window, across all six threat categories. Names the observations recorded but never evaluated because no threshold was on file.
fields.label: List Crop Observations

fields.description: READ. One tracked threat in full — first seen, peak, latest, trend, times over threshold — with its scouting history and every recommendation raised against it. The peak is not the latest: a pest answered in June still peaked in June, and next year's programme is planned off the peak.
fields.label: Get Pest Pressure

fields.description: READ. The board — every threat being tracked, worst first, ordered by the status ladder rather than by raw numbers that are in different units and cannot be ranked against each other.
fields.label: List Pest Pressures

fields.description: READ. One recommendation in full — what was seen, what number it crossed, every option with its control method, least chemical first, and what the mix scores. Rejected options are kept rather than deleted.
fields.label: Get IPM Recommendation

fields.description: READ. Score a set of control methods on this app's own 0-100 IPM scale — a hypothetical, one recommendation, or a whole block or season. NOT a certification: not USDA organic, not Protected Harvest, not IPM Institute. Writes nothing.
fields.label: Compute Sustainability Score

fields.description: WRITE. Write or revise a pest action threshold. The comparison is an argument, not an assumption — a Nutrient threshold fires BELOW its number. Revising retires the old row rather than editing it, so observations already evaluated still point at the number that evaluated them.
fields.label: Set Pest Action Threshold

fields.description: WRITE. File what a scout saw and run the threshold engine on it: records the observation, moves the block's pest pressure, and generates an IPM recommendation where the action threshold was crossed. A count over threshold with beneficials present at the threshold's ratio generates 'hold and re-scout' instead of a control.
fields.label: Create Crop Observation

fields.description: MUTATING. Sweeps one window of task completions and turns every closed scouting task into the Crop Observation it produced — the BBCH code, the Brix and its method off the task's stamped record data, and the location fix, the first photograph and the worker's findings off the assignment — running the threshold engine on it where it was a pest scout. It is a TOOL rather than a `doc_events` hook because this app promises to install none, and running it here means an operator can see it, switch it off and re-run it over last week. Idempotent on Crop Observation.source_task, so a second sweep over the same window writes nothing. OFF by default.
fields.label: Index Scouting Observations
Value Block Lifecycle — Plantings, Cost and Revenue

fields.description: READ. Plantings on file, newest plant year first. Reports establishing acres — the acreage currently consuming money and returning none, which no report built on a fiscal year will show.
fields.label: List Planting Seasons

fields.description: READ. One planting with where it stands in its own life, including leaf year and what the dates and the status say about each other.
fields.label: Get Planting Season

fields.description: READ. What one planting cost — from the ledger via its cost center, from the attribution register, and the overlap between them. Rows that are probably already inside the ledger figure are excluded from the total and named rather than silently included or dropped.
fields.label: Get Block Cost Summary

fields.description: READ. What one planting returned, and on what basis it was attributed. This is an ATTRIBUTION of revenue the ledger already recognised, not a recognition of it — it answers which ground earned the money, not what the business earned. Flags deliveries whose return has not been attributed back.
fields.label: Get Block Revenue Summary

fields.description: READ. Cost against return for one planting, read against its own lifecycle. An establishing block's negative margin is reported as investment carried in the block's basis, NOT as a loss. Pass cumulative for a perennial's whole life to date, which is the only honest way to read a block that takes years to pay back.
fields.label: Get Block Profitability

fields.description: WRITE. Open a planting — the junction between a block and what grows on it for a year. Perennial and annual are different shapes: an Annual whose plant year and season year differ is refused, because several years of establishment cost landing against one year's revenue makes a block read as ruinous in one season and free in the others.
fields.label: Create Planting Season

fields.description: READ. One employee bank account, or all of one employee's. Returns only the masked last four digits — never the full account number.
fields.label: Get Employee Bank Account

fields.description: READ. Employee bank accounts across the company, filtered by employee, status, or outstanding prenote. Returns only the masked last four digits.
fields.label: List Employee Bank Accounts

fields.description: MUTATING. Register where an employee's wages are deposited. The routing number is ABA check-digit validated; the account number is stored encrypted.
fields.label: Create Employee Bank Account

fields.description: MUTATING. Change one employee bank account. Changing the routing or account number clears the prenote flag.
fields.label: Update Employee Bank Account

fields.description: MUTATING. Build a NACHA ACH file from a calculated Farm Payroll Entry and attach it privately to that entry. THIS IS THE TOOL THAT MOVES WAGES.
fields.label: Generate NACHA File

fields.description: MUTATING. Build a zero-dollar NACHA prenotification file so the receiving banks can confirm the accounts exist before real wages are sent.
fields.label: Generate Prenote File
